1	# Cal.diy — Student Setup Guide (Windows-friendly)
2	
3	How to get this project running locally, tested with seed data, with unit + E2E tests — the exact path verified on Windows 11 (2026-07-16).

7	## What you need
8	
9	| Tool | Version we verified | Notes |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| Node.js | v24.x (repo requires >= 18) | |
12	| Yarn | 4.12.0 via Corepack | `yarn --version` inside the repo must say 4.12.0 |
13	| Docker Desktop | any recent | **Only needed for PostgreSQL + Mailhog.** The app itself runs natively. No local Postgres install required. |
14	| Git Bash | ships with Git for Windows | Run the setup commands below in Git Bash, not PowerShell |

16	Clone under a path with **no spaces or apostrophes** (e.g. `C:\dev\...`) — shell scripts in this monorepo break otherwise.
17	
18	> 💡 **New to Next.js?** Cal.diy's frontend and API routes are built with [Next.js 14](https://nextjs.org/docs). The [Next.js Getting Started tutorial](https://nextjs.org/learn) covers the App Router, server components, and API routes — the three things you'll encounter most.
19	
20	> 💡 **New to Prisma?** The database schema lives in `packages/prisma/schema.prisma`, and all queries go through the [Prisma Client](https://www.prisma.io/docs/getting-started). The [Prisma quickstart](https://www.prisma.io/docs/getting-started/quickstart-sqlite) explains the schema → migration → query workflow.

24	## Setup (first time)
25	
26	```bash
27	# 1. Clone (Windows: symlinks flag matters) and install
28	git clone -c core.symlinks=true https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy.git
29	cd cal.diy
30	yarn
31	
32	# 2. Environment file
33	cp .env.example .env
34	```
35	
36	Edit `.env` and set these two (generate values with the commands shown):
37	
38	```bash
39	openssl rand -base64 32   # -> NEXTAUTH_SECRET
40	openssl rand -base64 24   # -> CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY
41	```
42	
43	```bash
44	# 3. WINDOWS FIX — packages/prisma/.env is a broken symlink on most Windows clones
45	#    (it will be a tiny text file containing "../../.env"). Replace it with a real copy:
46	rm packages/prisma/.env && cp .env packages/prisma/.env
47	#    Re-do this copy whenever you change the root .env.
48	
49	# 4. Database (Docker): starts Postgres 18 on port 5450, migrates, seeds
50	yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-up
51	yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-deploy
52	yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-seed
53	
54	# 5. Mailhog (emails during dev/E2E) — http://localhost:8025
55	cd packages/emails && docker compose up -d && cd ../..
56	
57	# 6. Run the app
58	yarn dev
59	```

71	## Running tests
72	
73	### Unit tests (Vitest, ~2 min)
74	
75	```bash
76	NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E="" TZ=UTC yarn test
77	```
78	
79	**Why the `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=""` prefix:** if your `.env` has `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1` (needed for E2E), 7 unit tests fail by design — E2E mode intentionally bypasses SSRF localhost-blocking and forces feature rollouts to 100%. Blank it for unit runs.
80	
81	**Verified Windows baseline (2026-07-16): 4049 passed, 58 skipped.** Two files fail on Windows only (`\` path separators — they pass on Linux/CI): `apps/web/test/lib/next-config.test.ts` and `apps/web/test/lib/pagesAndRewritePaths.test.ts`. Safe to ignore.
82	
83	### E2E tests (Playwright)
84	
85	One-time: `npx playwright install` (downloads browsers) and set in `.env`: `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1`, `E2E_TEST_MAILHOG_ENABLED=1`.
86	
87	Two Windows realities to work around:
88	
89	1. **Don't run the full suite against `yarn dev`** — the dev-mode server hangs under parallel test load (verified: 120s navigation timeouts, then total unresponsiveness). Use a production build.
90	2. **Playwright can't auto-start the server on Windows** — the `webServer` command in `playwright.config.ts` uses Unix inline-env syntax (`NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1 yarn ...`) that cmd.exe can't parse (`Process from config.webServer was not able to start`). Start the server yourself in Git Bash; Playwright then reuses it (`reuseExistingServer` is on locally).
91	
92	```bash
93	# Terminal 1 — build once, then serve the production app (stop yarn dev first)
94	export NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=16384"
95	yarn build          # if it fails once on sprite.svg/Biome, just run it again (see gotchas)
96	yarn workspace @calcom/web copy-app-store-static
97	NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1 yarn workspace @calcom/web start -p 3000
98	
99	# Terminal 2 — re-seed and run the suite (headless, throttled workers)
100	yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-seed
101	PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS=1 NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1 yarn playwright test --project=@calcom/web --workers=4
102	```
103	
104	**Verified Windows baseline (2026-07-16): 243 passed, 3 failed, 27 skipped in ~6 min** (273 total). Known failures:
105	- `icons.e2e.ts` — no `win32` screenshot baseline exists in the repo (Linux-only snapshots); environment artifact, not a bug.
106	- 2 `booking-seats.e2e.ts` reschedule tests — timeouts/element-not-found; rerun individually before treating as real regressions.
107	
108	While developing, run a single spec instead of the whole suite:
109	`PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS=1 yarn e2e apps/web/playwright/login.e2e.ts`
110	
111	## Gotchas we actually hit (in order)
112	
113	1. **Port conflicts** — cal.diy needs 3000 (app), 5450 (Postgres), 8025/1025 (Mailhog). Check with `netstat -ano | findstr "3000 5450 8025"` and stop whatever holds them (for us it was another project's Docker container: `docker stop <name>`).
114	2. **`packages/prisma/.env` broken symlink** — every Prisma command fails with `unexpected character / in variable name` until you replace it with a real copy (step 3 above).
115	3. **`yarn build` fails once with a Biome error on `sprite.svg`** (`No files were processed in the specified paths`) — a CRLF/LF line-ending artifact of the Windows checkout. The failing step already rewrote the file, so **just run `yarn build` again**; it passes on the second run.
116	4. **Build memory** — export `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=16384"` (or 8192 on 16 GB machines) before `yarn build`/`yarn dev`.
117	5. **`NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1` breaks unit tests** — see the unit-test section above.
118	6. **Playwright webServer fails to start on Windows** — see the E2E section above.
119

124	yarn dev                              # http://localhost:3000
125	```
126	
127	Reset the database to a clean seeded state anytime: `yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-reset` (nukes the Docker volume, re-migrates, re-seeds).

129	## Contributing workflow
130	
131	All team members have write access to this repository, so the team uses a **branch-based** workflow — not forks. Here is the background and the commands.
132	
133	**Why not forks?** Forking is the standard model for contributing to open-source projects where you _don't_ have write access: you fork to your own GitHub account, clone your fork, and open a PR from your fork back to the original. You will encounter this when contributing to the upstream project. But for your course team — where everyone has write access to the shared repo — it just adds confusion: two clones on your machine, two remotes to keep in sync, merge conflicts that are harder to reason about.
134	
135	**Branch-based workflow** is what most professional teams use internally. You clone the shared repo once, create a short-lived branch for each issue, push the branch back to the same repo, and open a PR from that branch into `main`. One clone, one remote, full PR workflow.
136	
137	### For each issue you work on
138	
139	```bash
140	# One-time setup: clone the team repo (skip if already done)
141	git clone https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy.git
142	cd cal.diy
143	
144	# Before starting each issue: make sure you are on a fresh main
145	git checkout main
146	git pull origin main
147	
148	# Create a branch named for the issue
149	git checkout -b feat/issue-17-dark-mode      # new feature
150	git checkout -b fix/issue-42-toast-dismiss   # bug fix
151	
152	# ... make your changes, run tests ...
153	
154	# Stage and commit
155	git add <the files you changed>
156	git commit -m "feat: add dark mode toggle (#17)"
157	
158	# Push the branch to the team repo
159	git push origin feat/issue-17-dark-mode
160	```
161	
162	After pushing, GitHub shows a **"Compare & pull request"** banner on the repository page. Click it to open a PR from your branch into `main`. Fill in the description (what changed and why), reference the issue (`Closes #17`), and request a review from a teammate.
163	
164	**Branch naming:**
165	
166	| Prefix | Use for |
167	|---|---|
168	| `feat/issue-<N>-short-description` | new features |
169	| `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` | bug fixes |
170	| `chore/short-description` | docs, config, dependency updates |
171	
172	> ⚠️ **`main` is protected — direct pushes are blocked.** All changes go through a reviewed PR. If you accidentally commit to `main` locally, move your changes to a branch before pushing:
173	>
174	> ```bash
175	> git checkout -b fix/issue-42-my-fix   # create branch from your current state
176	> git checkout main
177	> git reset --hard origin/main          # revert local main to match remote
178	> ```
179	
180	**After your PR is merged**, delete the branch to keep the repo tidy:
181	
182	```bash
183	git checkout main
184	git pull origin main
185	git branch -d feat/issue-17-dark-mode
186	```

## Exact steps to run the codebase

**Prereqs:** Node 24.x, Docker Desktop running, Git Bash (not PowerShell), repo cloned to a path with no spaces/apostrophes.

```bash
# 1. Install deps (yarn --version must report 4.12.0 via Corepack)
yarn

# 2. Env file
cp .env.example .env
```

Then edit `.env` and fill in two secrets:
```bash
openssl rand -base64 32   # -> NEXTAUTH_SECRET
openssl rand -base64 24   # -> CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY
```

```bash
# 3. Windows fix — packages/prisma/.env is a broken symlink; make it a real copy
rm packages/prisma/.env && cp .env packages/prisma/.env

# 4. Database: Postgres 18 on port 5450, then migrate + seed
yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-up
yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-deploy
yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-seed

# 5. Mailhog for dev emails (http://localhost:8025)
cd packages/emails && docker compose up -d && cd ../..

# 6. Raise build memory, then run
export NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=16384"   # 8192 on a 16 GB machine
yarn dev
```

App at **http://localhost:3000**. Log in as `pro@example.com` / `pro`, `free@example.com` / `free`, or `admin@example.com` / `ADMINadmin2022!`.

**Every day after that** — just two commands:
```bash
yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-up   # if the container isn't already up
yarn dev
```

## Three things that will bite you

1. **Step 3 is not optional.** Without it every Prisma command dies with `unexpected character / in variable name`. Redo the copy any time you edit the root `.env`.
2. **Ports 3000 / 5450 / 8025 / 1025 must be free** — `netstat -ano | findstr "3000 5450 8025"`, then `docker stop <name>` on whatever's squatting.
3. **`yarn build` fails the first time** on a `sprite.svg` Biome error (CRLF artifact). The failed run already rewrote the file — just run it again.

## Tests, briefly

- **Unit:** `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E="" TZ=UTC yarn test` — the blank prefix matters; E2E mode makes 7 tests fail by design. Baseline 4049 passed; 2 files fail on Windows only (path separators), safe to ignore.
- **E2E:** needs a production build in one terminal and the suite in another, because dev-mode hangs under parallel load and Playwright's `webServer` can't self-start on Windows. Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1` + `E2E_TEST_MAILHOG_ENABLED=1` in `.env` first, and remember to flip `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E` back before running unit tests.

Useful extras: `yarn db-studio` (Prisma Studio on 5555) to browse data, `yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-reset` to nuke and re-seed.

Per [students.md](students.md#L24-L34), the exact steps:

```bash
# 1. Clone (Windows: symlinks flag matters)
git clone -c core.symlinks=true https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy.git
cd cal.diy

# 2. Install deps
yarn
```

**Prerequisites before running `yarn`:**
- Node.js v24.x (repo requires ≥18)
- Yarn 4.12.0 via Corepack — verify with `yarn --version` inside the repo, must print `4.12.0`
- Run this in **Git Bash**, not PowerShell
- Clone path must have **no spaces or apostrophes** (e.g. `C:\dev\...`) or shell scripts in the monorepo break

That's it for the dependency install itself — `yarn` at the repo root installs everything across the monorepo workspaces. The next step in the guide is the `.env` file setup, not more deps.

That's a known corepack/Node compatibility bug, not something in your repo — the bundled `yarn.js` fails when run under Node v22.14.0 with an ESM `require` shim error. Two likely fixes:

1. **Update corepack itself** (fixes an ESM-loader bug in older corepack releases):
```bash
npm install -g corepack@latest
corepack prepare yarn@4.12.0 --activate
```

2. **Or switch to Node v24.x** — that's the version the guide verified against (`students.md` line 11), and yours is v22.14.0. If you have nvm-windows or fnm installed, switching versions may sidestep this entirely.

Want me to try option 1 first (update corepack), or do you already know which Node version manager you're using so I can guide the switch?

what is the reason for running this command?

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-08 04:23:12Z)**_

Two separate reasons, one per line of the command:

1. **`export PATH="/c/Users/jko06/node24:$PATH"`** — Your system's installed Node is v22.14.0, but running `yarn` (any way we tried — corepack-activated, ad-hoc, on both v22 and v24) kept hitting a `Dynamic require of "util" is not supported` crash from a broken corepack-downloaded copy of yarn. This line puts a clean, portable Node v24.20.0 (the version [students.md](students.md#L11) says was actually verified) first in `PATH` for just this terminal session — no system changes, no admin rights needed.

2. **`node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs install`** — Instead of running plain `yarn` (which resolves to corepack's broken downloaded `yarn.js`), this runs the working copy of yarn that's already vendored inside the repo at `.yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs` (referenced by `.yarnrc.yml`'s `yarnPath` setting). That file is CommonJS, not ESM, so it doesn't trip the same bug. `install` is the actual dependency-install step — equivalent to what `students.md` step 1 calls simply `yarn`.

So: line 1 works around a broken Node/corepack combo on your machine, line 2 does the real work (installing all the monorepo's dependencies) using a copy of yarn that isn't affected by that bug.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-08 04:31:27Z)**_

That's normal for a first install on this repo — cal.com's monorepo has many workspaces, patched dependencies, and postinstall scripts (Prisma client generation, husky hooks, etc.), so **5–15 minutes** isn't unusual on a first run, especially over a slower connection or on Windows disk I/O.

A few things to check if you're unsure whether it's actually working or stuck:

1. **Is there any output?** Yarn usually prints progress like `➤ YN0000: ┌ Resolution step` / `Fetch step` / `Link step`. If you see any of these lines updating, it's working.
2. **Check Task Manager** — look for `node.exe` using CPU or network activity. If it's using resources, it's still working.
3. **No output at all for 15+ minutes with 0% CPU/network** — that would suggest it's actually hung (possibly waiting on a network timeout), and Ctrl+C to cancel and retry would be reasonable.

What does your terminal currently show — is there progress output, or has it gone silent?

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-08 14:24:03Z)**_

No — you don't need a Docker account to run Docker Desktop locally. It'll prompt you to sign in on first launch, but you can skip/close that dialog and use it anonymously.

The only reason you'd ever want one: Docker Hub applies pull rate limits to anonymous (unauthenticated) image pulls. For this project you're only pulling a couple of images (Postgres, Mailhog) once, so you're very unlikely to hit that limit — a free account isn't necessary.

Once Docker Desktop is open and running (check the whale icon in your system tray is not showing "starting..."), let me know and we'll move to the database step:

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-08 14:31:20Z)**_

Here's the complete list, reflecting what we actually ran (including the Windows/corepack workaround) rather than the plain `yarn`/`yarn dev` in [students.md](students.md).

## One-time setup (already done)

```bash
# 1. Clone (Windows: symlinks flag matters)
git clone -c core.symlinks=true https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy.git
cd cal.diy

# 2. Install deps — using the vendored yarn .cjs + portable Node 24
#    (works around a corepack/yarn@4.12.0 ESM bug on Windows)
export PATH="/c/Users/jko06/node24:$PATH"
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs install

# 3. Environment file
cp .env.example .env
# then edit .env, setting:
#   NEXTAUTH_SECRET       -> openssl rand -base64 32
#   CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY -> openssl rand -base64 24

# 4. Windows fix — replace broken prisma/.env symlink with a real copy
rm packages/prisma/.env && cp .env packages/prisma/.env

# 5. Database (Docker Desktop must be running)
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs workspace @calcom/prisma db-up
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs workspace @calcom/prisma db-deploy
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs workspace @calcom/prisma db-seed

# 6. Mailhog (dev emails) — http://localhost:8025
cd packages/emails && docker compose up -d && cd ../..
```

## Run the app (what you're about to do)

```bash
export PATH="/c/Users/jko06/node24:$PATH"
export NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=16384"
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs dev
```

App: **http://localhost:3000** — logins: `pro@example.com`/`pro`, `free@example.com`/`free`, `admin@example.com`/`ADMINadmin2022!`

## Daily workflow (every day after today)

```bash
export PATH="/c/Users/jko06/node24:$PATH"

# if the Postgres container isn't already running
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs workspace @calcom/prisma db-up

# then start the app
export NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=16384"
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs dev
```

**Note:** every place `students.md` says plain `yarn <command>`, substitute `node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs <command>` (with the `PATH` export at the top of your session) — that's the one durable change from the documented steps, needed only because of the corepack bug on your machine. Everything else matches the guide exactly.

_**User (2026-09-08 14:39:16Z)**_

what are the commands to make the application stop running

---

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-08 14:39:21Z)**_

**Stop the dev server:** in the terminal where `yarn dev` is running, press `Ctrl+C`.

**Stop the background services (optional — only if you want to free up ports/resources):**

```bash
# Stop Postgres
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs workspace @calcom/prisma db-stop

# Stop Mailhog
cd packages/emails && docker compose down && cd ../..
```

If `db-stop` isn't a defined script, the equivalent is:
```bash
cd packages/prisma && docker compose down && cd ../..
```

You don't need to stop Postgres/Mailhog between sessions — leaving them running is fine and is what [students.md](students.md#L120-L125)'s daily workflow assumes (`db-up` is a no-op if it's already running). Only stop them if you want to reclaim ports 5450/8025/1025, or before shutting down your machine.

- **Stop Postgres/Mailhog:** run the `docker compose down` / `db-stop` commands in a Git Bash terminal from the repo root, same as the setup commands.

const vitestMode = process.env.VITEST_MODE;
// Support both new VITEST_MODE env var and legacy CLI flags for backwards compatibility
// The CLI flags are passed through but Vitest 4.0 doesn't reject them when using yarn test
const isPackagedEmbedMode = vitestMode === "packaged-embed" || process.argv.includes("--packaged-embed-tests-only");
const isIntegrationMode = vitestMode === "integration" || process.argv.includes("--integrationTestsOnly");
const isTimezoneMode = vitestMode === "timezone" || process.argv.includes("--timeZoneDependentTestsOnly");

// Always set INTEGRATION_TEST_MODE to allow server-side imports in jsdom environment
// This is needed because getBookingFields.ts checks for this env var to allow imports
process.env.INTEGRATION_TEST_MODE = "true";

if (isTimezoneMode && !process.env.TZ) {
  throw new Error("TZ environment variable is not set for timezone tests");
}

function getTestInclude() {
  if (isPackagedEmbedMode) {
    return ["packages/embeds/**/packaged/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,js}"];
  }
  if (isIntegrationMode) {
    return ["packages/**/*.integration-test.ts", "apps/**/*.integration-test.ts"];
  }
  if (isTimezoneMode) {
    return ["packages/**/*.timezone.test.ts", "apps/**/*.timezone.test.ts"];
  }
  // Default: run all test files (Vitest default pattern)
  return ["**/*.{test,spec}.{js,mjs,cjs,ts,mts,cts,jsx,tsx}"];
}

function getTestExclude() {
  const baseExclude = [
    "**/node_modules/**",
    "**/dist/**",
    "apps/api/v2/**/*.spec.ts",
    "__checks__/**/*.spec.ts",
  ];
  if (isIntegrationMode || isTimezoneMode) {
    return [...baseExclude, "packages/embeds/**/*"];
  }
  return baseExclude;
}

That's very likely the cause: you have only ~2GB free out of 16GB RAM right now, and this repo's Vitest defaults to spawning up to **20 parallel forks** (one per logical CPU) — each running a jsdom + Next.js-loaded environment. That's severe memory pressure that can cause forked workers to crash/corrupt mid-run, which is consistent with widespread, non-deterministic-looking failures across otherwise-passing test files.

Two things worth trying:

1. **Close memory-heavy apps** (browser tabs, IDE windows, Docker Desktop if you don't need it mid-run) to free RAM before testing.
2. **Limit Vitest's parallelism** so it doesn't try to run 20 forks at once:

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-08 18:21:32Z)**_

My mistake — `db-stop` doesn't exist. Use plain Docker Compose instead:

```bash
cd packages/prisma && docker compose down && cd ../..
```

That stops the Postgres container without removing the data volume, so it'll still be there next time you run `db-up`. (If you ever want to wipe and reseed from scratch, `db-nuke` or `db-reset` does that instead — but don't run those unless you actually want to lose local data.)

_**User (2026-09-14 23:22:36Z)**_

can i use the terminal instead of git bash

---

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-14 23:22:51Z)**_

You can, but with caveats — [students.md](students.md#L14) recommends Git Bash specifically because some of what we've been running uses Unix-only syntax that PowerShell doesn't support (e.g. `export PATH=...`, inline env vars like `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E="" TZ=UTC yarn test`, and `/c/Users/...`-style paths).

For a simple case like stopping Docker containers, PowerShell works fine as-is since it's just calling `docker`/`docker compose` directly, no bash syntax involved:

```powershell
cd packages/prisma
docker compose down
cd ../..
```

But for anything involving our Node 24/yarn workaround or the test commands, you'd need PowerShell syntax instead, e.g.:

```powershell
$env:PATH = "C:\Users\jko06\node24;$env:PATH"
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs dev
```

and env-var-prefixed commands become two lines instead of one (`$env:VAR = "value"` then the command, since PowerShell has no inline `VAR=value cmd` syntax).

My recommendation: stick with Git Bash for anything yarn/node/testing-related, since that's what's been verified to work end-to-end — but plain `docker` commands are safe in either shell.

what are the commands to run the test suite

---

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-14 23:31:57Z)**_

Here's the full set, adjusted for your machine (Node 24 workaround + limited worker count due to available RAM).

## Unit tests (Vitest, ~2–3 min)

```bash
export PATH="/c/Users/jko06/node24:$PATH"
export NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=""
export TZ=UTC
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs vitest run --maxWorkers=4
```

We confirmed this gives **4057 passed, 1 failed (known Windows path-separator issue), 58 skipped** — matches the guide's verified baseline. Without `--maxWorkers=4` it fails widely on your machine due to RAM pressure from 20 parallel forks, so always include that flag here.

## E2E tests (Playwright)

One-time setup if you haven't done it: install browsers and enable E2E mode in `.env`.
```bash
export PATH="/c/Users/jko06/node24:$PATH"
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs playwright install
```
Then in `.env`, set `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1` and `E2E_TEST_MAILHOG_ENABLED=1`.

**Terminal 1** — build and serve a production build (don't run against `yarn dev` — it hangs under E2E load per [students.md](students.md#L89)):
```bash
export PATH="/c/Users/jko06/node24:$PATH"
export NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=16384"
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs build          # if it fails once on sprite.svg, just run again
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs workspace @calcom/web copy-app-store-static
NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1 node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs workspace @calcom/web start -p 3000
```

**Terminal 2** — reseed and run the suite:
```bash
export PATH="/c/Users/jko06/node24:$PATH"
node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs workspace @calcom/prisma db-seed
PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS=1 NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1 node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs playwright test --project=@calcom/web --workers=4
```

To run a single spec while developing instead of the whole E2E suite:
```bash
PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS=1 node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs playwright test apps/web/playwright/login.e2e.ts
```

Want me to run the unit tests again to reconfirm, or move on to E2E setup?

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 00:05:50Z)**_

This is **cal.diy** — a student fork of [cal.com](https://cal.com), an open-source scheduling platform (Calendly alternative). It's a large **Turborepo + Yarn workspaces monorepo**.

## Top-level layout

```
cal.diy/
├── apps/          → deployable applications
├── packages/      → shared libraries consumed by the apps
├── docs/          → project documentation
├── scripts/       → build/dev tooling scripts
├── specs/         → spec files
├── deploy/        → deployment configs
├── example-apps/  → sample integrations
└── (config files: turbo.json, vitest.config.mts, playwright.config.ts, biome.json, etc.)
```

## `apps/` — the three deployables

| App | What it is |
|---|---|
| **`web`** | The main Next.js 14 app — the actual product (booking pages, dashboard, event types, settings). Uses both the Pages Router (`pages/`) and App Router (`app/`) side by side, plus `modules/`, `components/`, `server/` for app-specific logic. |
| **`api`** | The public REST API — `v2/` is the current NestJS-based version. |
| **`docs`** | The documentation site. |

## `packages/` — shared code, 20 workspaces

The most important ones:

- **`features/`** — the real business logic, organized by domain: `bookings/`, `availability/`, `schedules/`, `webhooks/`, `calendars/`, `calendar-subscription/`, `credits/`, `flags/` (feature flags), `di/` (dependency injection), `watchlist/`, `onboarding/`, etc. This is where most product logic lives, shared between `web` and `api`.
- **`app-store/`** — the integrations marketplace (152+ entries: `applecalendar`, `alby`, `amie`, etc.), each a self-contained integration package plus generated registry files (`*.generated.ts`) that stitch them together.
- **`prisma/`** — the database layer: `schema.prisma`, migrations (595 of them), seed scripts. This is what `students.md`'s `db-up`/`db-deploy`/`db-seed` commands operate on.
- **`trpc/`** — tRPC routers (type-safe API layer between client and server).
- **`ui/`** — the shared design-system components (buttons, inputs, selects — what we saw failing/passing in the Vitest run earlier).
- **`lib/`** — general shared utilities.
- **`emails/`** — transactional email templates (this is what pairs with Mailhog in local dev).
- **`embeds/`** — the embeddable booking widget.
- **`platform/`** — the "Platform" product (Cal.com-as-a-platform / white-label API for other companies).
- **`i18n/`** — internationalization/translation infra.
- **`kysely/`, `dayjs/`, `sms/`, `debugging/`, `coss-ui/`, `types/`, `tsconfig/`, `config/`, `testing/`** — smaller focused utility packages (shared TS configs, date handling, test setup like the `setupVitest.ts` we debugged earlier, shared types).

## How it fits together

- **Turborepo** (`turbo.json`) orchestrates builds/tests across all these workspaces with caching and task dependencies.
- **Yarn 4 (Berry)** workspaces (`.yarnrc.yml`, `yarn.lock`) manage the dependency graph — one `node_modules`, one lockfile for the whole repo.
- **Prisma** is the single source of truth for the DB schema, consumed by both `apps/web` and `apps/api`.
- **Vitest** (root `vitest.config.mts` + `vitest.workspace.ts`) runs unit tests across all packages/apps at once — which is exactly the suite we ran together for [students.md](students.md).
- **Playwright** (`playwright.config.ts`) runs E2E tests against the built `web` app.

If you want, I can go a level deeper into any one area — e.g. how `apps/web` routes map to `packages/features`, or how the app-store integration pattern works — just point me at what you're trying to understand or build.

No — there's no unsaved-changes warning anywhere in this codebase, for event types or any other form.

**What exists:**
- `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx:279` uses `formMethods.formState.isDirty` to enable/disable the Save button — that's the only place dirty-state is used.

**Result:** if a user edits an event type's setup and navigates away (tab switch, sidebar link, browser close/refresh) without clicking Save, their changes are silently lost — no confirmation prompt of any kind.

If you're looking to add this, the natural hook points are:
- **In-app navigation**: intercept clicks in `EventTypeLayout.tsx` (or wherever the tab/sidebar links live) when `formMethods.formState.isDirty` is true, and show a confirmation dialog before navigating.
- **Browser close/refresh**: a `useEffect` adding a `beforeunload` listener conditioned on `isDirty`.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 00:13:57Z)**_

It's more approachable than I expected — and there's a relevant wrinkle: this repo's `package.json` actually pins **Next.js 16.2.3** (not 14, despite what `students.md` says), and Next 16's `<Link>` component ships an `onNavigate` prop specifically for intercepting/canceling navigation. That changes the picture.

**Easy part (~15–30 min): browser tab close/refresh**
Add a `useEffect` in `EventType.tsx` that registers a `beforeunload` listener whenever `formMethods.formState.isDirty` is true. Small, self-contained, no shared-component changes.

**Medium part (~1–2 hours): switching between the event-type's own sub-tabs** (Setup/Availability/Limits/Advanced/etc.)
Good news: those tabs already render via `next/link`'s `<Link>` in `packages/ui/components/navigation/tabs/{Horizontal,Vertical}TabItem.tsx`. I'd need to:
1. Add an `onNavigate` passthrough prop to those two shared tab components (low risk — optional prop, backward compatible).
2. In `EventTypeLayout.tsx`, wire a handler that checks `isDirty` and shows a confirm dialog before allowing the switch.
3. Update `navigation.test.tsx` for the new prop.

**Harder, and easy to leave out of scope: everything else** — the main sidebar ("Bookings", "Availability" top-level nav), browser back/forward, breadcrumbs, the command palette (Cmd+K). Next 16's `onNavigate` only fires for that specific `<Link>`; it doesn't give you a single global "block all navigation" hook. Covering every exit path would mean threading the same check into every nav trigger across the app — a much bigger, cross-cutting change.

**My honest take:** a scoped version — beforeunload + the event-type's own tab-switching — is a genuinely small, mergeable PR (roughly half a day including tests). Full "warn no matter how you leave" coverage is a noticeably bigger job. Want me to implement the scoped version?

## Findings

**1. Sidebar component location**

- Layout: `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/(main-nav)/layout.tsx` — a server component that renders `<Shell withoutMain={true}>{children}</Shell>` around all pages in the `(main-nav)` group.
- `Shell`: `apps/web/modules/shell/Shell.tsx` — client component; renders `<SideBarContainer>` (desktop) and `<MobileNavigationContainer>` (mobile) alongside `<MainContainer>{children}</MainContainer>`.
- Sidebar chrome: `apps/web/modules/shell/SideBar.tsx` (`SideBarContainer`/`SideBar`) — renders `<Navigation />`.
- Nav items array + rendering: `apps/web/modules/shell/navigation/Navigation.tsx` (defines `getNavigationItems()` with `event_types_page_title`, `bookings`, `availability`, `apps`, `more`) and `apps/web/modules/shell/navigation/NavigationItem.tsx` (renders each item).

**2. Navigation mechanism**

All items — desktop (`NavigationItem`), mobile bottom bar (`MobileNavigationItem`), and mobile "more" sheet (`MobileNavigationMoreItem`) — render via `next/link`'s `<Link href={item.href} ...>`, not `router.push()`. Child items (e.g. Apps submenu) also use `<Link>`. This means `next/link`'s `onNavigate` prop is available at each `<Link>` call site for interception — but it would have to be added at three separate render sites (`NavigationItem.tsx` for all three link variants) since there's no single shared "navigate" function today.

**3. Shared layout, not per-page**

Yes — `(main-nav)/layout.tsx` wraps all pages in that route group with a single `Shell`/`SideBarContainer`/`Navigation` instance, per standard App Router layout semantics. The sidebar does NOT re-render/remount per page navigation within the group (event-types, bookings, availability, apps all share it). So the event-type edit page (`EventType.tsx`, deep under `event-types/[type]`) cannot pass `isDirty` as a prop to `Navigation.tsx` — they're siblings under the same layout, not parent/child.

**4. No existing unsaved-changes plumbing**

Searched for `NavigationContext`, `useUnsavedChangesGuard`, `useBlocker`, `beforePopState`, `routeChangeStart` — none exist. No global "form dirty" context wraps the main-nav layout currently. However, `packages/ui/components/dialog/ConfirmationDialogContent.tsx` (exported via `packages/ui/components/dialog/index.ts`) is a ready-made confirm-dialog primitive that could be reused for the "unsaved changes" prompt.

**What would need to change:** introduce a new React context/provider (e.g. `UnsavedChangesProvider`) at the `(main-nav)` layout or `Shell` level, exposing a `setIsDirty`/`registerGuard` setter that `EventType.tsx` calls via `useEffect` on `formState.isDirty` changes, and a consumer in `NavigationItem.tsx`'s `<Link>` `onClick`/`onNavigate` handlers that checks the context flag and opens `ConfirmationDialogContent` before allowing navigation.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 00:29:49Z)**_

Here's the concrete picture for warning on sidebar navigation (Bookings/Availability/Apps) specifically:

## Why it's harder than the tab-switching case

The sidebar (`apps/web/modules/shell/navigation/Navigation.tsx` + `NavigationItem.tsx`) is rendered **once**, in a layout (`(main-nav)/layout.tsx`) that wraps *every* page in that section — event types, bookings, availability, apps all share the same sidebar instance. The event-type edit form and the sidebar are siblings under that shared layout, not parent/child. So you can't just pass `isDirty` down as a prop — there's no direct line between "this form is dirty" and "this sidebar link was clicked."

## What it would take

1. **A shared context** (e.g. `UnsavedChangesProvider`) mounted at the `Shell`/`(main-nav)` layout level, exposing something like `setIsDirty(bool)`.
2. **`EventType.tsx`** calls that setter in a `useEffect` whenever `formMethods.formState.isDirty` changes.
3. **`NavigationItem.tsx`** (and its two siblings — there's a separate mobile bottom-bar item and a mobile "more" sheet item, so **three** render sites) reads that context and, on click/`onNavigate`, checks the flag and shows a confirm dialog before letting the `<Link>` navigate.
4. The confirm dialog itself doesn't need to be built — `packages/ui/components/dialog/ConfirmationDialogContent.tsx` already exists and is exactly this kind of primitive.

## Feasibility verdict

**Moderate, not hard** — nothing here is exotic, but it's a genuine cross-cutting change: one new context provider, one new consumer wired into 3 link-rendering components, plus remembering to clear the dirty flag on successful save/unmount so stale warnings don't leak onto other pages. Realistically **half a day to a day** of work including testing (there's already a `navigation.test.tsx` for these components that would need updates).

The main risk isn't difficulty, it's **scope creep**: once this context exists, it's tempting to also guard the browser back button, the command palette, and event-type-list clicks — those are separate call sites too, but each one is now just "another place to check the context flag," so the marginal cost per additional guard point is small once the core plumbing is in.

Want me to implement this (context + wiring into the sidebar's three link components + the event-type form), or start smaller with just the sidebar case exactly as you described?

import { cookies, headers } from "next/headers";
import { redirect } from "next/navigation";

import { checkOnboardingRedirect } from "@calcom/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils";
import { getServerSession } from "@calcom/features/auth/lib/getServerSession";

import { buildLegacyRequest } from "@lib/buildLegacyCtx";

const RedirectPage = async () => {
  const session = await getServerSession({ req: buildLegacyRequest(await headers(), await cookies()) });

  if (!session?.user?.id) {
    redirect("/auth/login");
  }

  // Check if user needs onboarding and redirect before going to event-types
  const organizationId = session.user.profile?.organizationId ?? null;
  const onboardingPath = await checkOnboardingRedirect(session.user.id, {
    checkEmailVerification: true,
    organizationId,
  });
  if (onboardingPath) {
    redirect(onboardingPath);
  }

  redirect("/event-types");
};

export default RedirectPage;

=== onboardingUtils ===
packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts
import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
import { FeaturesRepository } from "@calcom/features/flags/features.repository";
import { MembershipRepository } from "@calcom/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository";
import { ProfileRepository } from "@calcom/features/profile/repositories/ProfileRepository";
import { UserRepository } from "@calcom/features/users/repositories/UserRepository";
import { prisma } from "@calcom/prisma";

const ONBOARDING_INTRODUCED_AT = dayjs("September 1 2021").toISOString();

/**
 * Checks if a user needs onboarding on the server side.
 * Returns the onboarding path if redirect is needed, null otherwise.
 *
 * @param userId - The user ID to check
 * @param options - Optional configuration
 * @param options.checkEmailVerification - Whether to check if email verification is required
 * @param options.organizationId - Optional organizationId from session (to avoid extra query)
 */
export async function checkOnboardingRedirect(
  userId: number,
  options?: {
    checkEmailVerification?: boolean;
    organizationId?: number | null;
  }
): Promise<string | null> {
  // Query user data needed for onboarding check using UserRepository
  const userRepository = new UserRepository(prisma);
  const user = await userRepository.findById({ id: userId });

  if (!user) {
    return null;
  }

  // Use provided organizationId or query it via ProfileRepository
  let organizationId: number | null;
  if (options?.organizationId !== undefined) {
    organizationId = options.organizationId;
  } else {
    const profile = await ProfileRepository.findFirstForUserId({ userId });
    organizationId = profile?.organizationId ?? null;
  }

  // Check if user should be shown onboarding
  const shouldShowOnboarding =
    !user.completedOnboarding && !organizationId && dayjs(user.createdDate).isAfter(ONBOARDING_INTRODUCED_AT);

  if (!shouldShowOnboarding) {
    return null;
  }

  // Check email verification if needed
  const featuresRepository = new FeaturesRepository(prisma);

  if (options?.checkEmailVerification) {
    const emailVerificationEnabled =
      await featuresRepository.checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally("email-verification");

    if (!user.emailVerified && user.identityProvider === "CAL" && emailVerificationEnabled) {
      // User needs email verification, redirect to verification page
      return "/auth/verify-email";
    }
  }

  // Determine which onboarding path to use
  const onboardingV3Enabled = await featuresRepository.checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally("onboarding-v3");

  // Check for any team membership (pending or accepted) to handle users who signed up via invite token
  // When users sign up with an invite token, the membership is auto-accepted
  const hasTeamMembership = await MembershipRepository.hasAnyTeamMembershipByUserId({ userId });

  if (hasTeamMembership && onboardingV3Enabled) {
    return "/onboarding/personal/settings";
  }

  return onboardingV3Enabled ? "/onboarding/getting-started" : "/getting-started";
}

model User {
  id                  Int                  @id @default(autoincrement())

  name                String?

  email               String

  travelSchedules     TravelSchedule[]

  bufferTime          Int                  @default(0)
  hideBranding        Boolean              @default(false)

  theme               String?
  appTheme            String?
  createdDate         DateTime             @default(now()) @map(name: "created")
  trialEndsAt         DateTime?
  lastActiveAt        DateTime?
  eventTypes          EventType[]          @relation("user_eventtype")
  credentials         Credential[]
  teams               Membership[]
  bookings            Booking[]
  schedules           Schedule[]
  defaultScheduleId   Int?
  selectedCalendars   SelectedCalendar[]
  completedOnboarding Boolean              @default(false)
  locale              String?
  timeFormat          Int?                 @default(12)
  twoFactorSecret     String?
  twoFactorEnabled    Boolean              @default(false)
  backupCodes         String?
  identityProvider    IdentityProvider     @default(CAL)
  identityProviderId  String?
  availability        Availability[]
  invitedTo           Int?
  webhooks            Webhook[]
  brandColor          String?
  darkBrandColor      String?
  // the location where the events will end up
  destinationCalendar DestinationCalendar?
  // participate in dynamic group booking or not
  allowDynamicBooking Boolean?             @default(true)

  // participate in SEO indexing or not
  allowSEOIndexing Boolean? @default(true)

  // receive monthly digest email for teams or not
  receiveMonthlyDigestEmail       Boolean? @default(true)
  // require email verification when someone books using your email
  requiresBookerEmailVerification Boolean? @default(false)

  /// @zod.import(["import { userMetadata } from '../../zod-utils'"]).custom.use(userMetadata)
  metadata           Json?
  verified           Boolean?           @default(false)
  role               UserPermissionRole @default(USER)
  apiKeys            ApiKey[]
  accounts           Account[]
  sessions           Session[]
  Feedback           Feedback[]
  ownedEventTypes    EventType[]        @relation("owner")
  verifiedNumbers    VerifiedNumber[]
  verifiedEmails     VerifiedEmail[]
  hosts              Host[]
  // organizationId is deprecated. Instead, rely on the Profile to search profiles by organizationId and then get user from the profile.
  organizationId     Int?
  organization       Team?              @relation("scope", fields: [organizationId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  accessCodes        AccessCode[]
  bookingRedirects   OutOfOfficeEntry[]
  bookingRedirectsTo OutOfOfficeEntry[] @relation(name: "toUser")

  // Used to lock the user account
  locked                         Boolean                       @default(false)
  platformOAuthClients           PlatformOAuthClient[]
  AccessToken                    AccessToken[]
  RefreshToken                   RefreshToken[]
  PlatformAuthorizationToken     PlatformAuthorizationToken[]
  profiles                       Profile[]
  movedToProfileId               Int?

  secondaryEmails                SecondaryEmail[]
  isPlatformManaged              Boolean                       @default(false)
  OutOfOfficeReasons             OutOfOfficeReason[]
  smsLockState                   SMSLockState                  @default(UNLOCKED)
  smsLockReviewedByAdmin         Boolean                       @default(false)
  NotificationsSubscriptions     NotificationsSubscriptions[]
  referralLinkId                 String?
  features                       UserFeatures[]
  reassignedBookings             Booking[]                     @relation("reassignByUser")
  createdAttributeToUsers        AttributeToUser[]             @relation("createdBy")
  updatedAttributeToUsers        AttributeToUser[]             @relation("updatedBy")
  createdTranslations            EventTypeTranslation[]        @relation("CreatedEventTypeTranslations")
  updatedTranslations            EventTypeTranslation[]        @relation("UpdatedEventTypeTranslations")
  reportedBookings               BookingReport[]               @relation("ReportedBy")
  wrongAssignmentReports         WrongAssignmentReport[]       @relation("WrongAssignmentReportedBy")
  reviewedWrongAssignmentReports WrongAssignmentReport[]       @relation("WrongAssignmentReviewedBy")
  BookingInternalNote            BookingInternalNote[]
  creationSource                 CreationSource?
  createdOrganizationOnboardings OrganizationOnboarding[]      @relation("CreatedOrganizationOnboardings")
  filterSegments                 FilterSegment[]
  filterSegmentPreferences       UserFilterSegmentPreference[]
  creditBalance                  CreditBalance?
  calAiPhoneNumbers              CalAiPhoneNumber[]
  agents                         Agent[]
  oAuthClients                   OAuthClient[]
  holidaySettings                UserHolidaySettings?

  autoOptInFeatures Boolean @default(false)

  @@unique([email])
  @@unique([email, username])
  @@unique([username, organizationId])
  @@unique([movedToProfileId])
  @@index([username])
  @@index([emailVerified])
  @@index([identityProvider])
  @@index([identityProviderId])
  @@map(name: "users")
}

## Findings

**1. Redirect logic — confirmed hardcoded, single entry point**

`apps/web/app/page.tsx` (root `/`) is the only post-login redirect logic — no `middleware.ts` exists in `apps/web` (only unrelated middleware in `apps/api/v2` and tRPC). Flow:

```
no session → redirect("/auth/login")
checkOnboardingRedirect(...) → if truthy, redirect there
otherwise → redirect("/event-types")   // literal, hardcoded string
```

`/event-types` is a **hardcoded literal**, not computed from any user field. `checkOnboardingRedirect` (`packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts`) is the only conditional branch — it checks `completedOnboarding`, org membership, email verification, and feature flags (`onboarding-v3`) to send new/unverified/invited users to `/auth/verify-email`, `/onboarding/getting-started`, `/onboarding/personal/settings`, or `/getting-started` instead. This is the one complication a new setting must coexist with: onboarding must still take priority over any custom landing page.

NextAuth's `redirect` callback (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:1165`) only validates same-origin callback URLs; it does not choose the landing page.

**2. Existing metadata infrastructure — reusable pattern already exists**

`User.metadata` is a `Json?` column (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma`) validated by `userMetadata` zod schema in `packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts:379`. It already stores flexible per-user preferences like `defaultConferencingApp` and `defaultBookerLayouts` — direct precedent for a `defaultLandingPage`/`homeView` field. No dedicated `landingPage`/`homeView` field exists today.

**3. Settings UI pattern**

`apps/web/modules/settings/my-account/general-view.tsx` is the template: react-hook-form + `Select`/`SettingsToggle` components, mutating via `trpc.viewer.me.updateProfile` or a dedicated mutation. `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/apps/updateUserDefaultConferencingApp.handler.ts` shows the exact pattern for a single metadata-field mutation: `userMetadata.parse(ctx.user.metadata)` → spread + overwrite key → `prisma.user.update`.

## What would need to be built
- Add `defaultLandingPage` (or similar) optional field to `userMetadata` zod schema (`packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts`) — no Prisma migration needed since it's stored in existing JSON `metadata` column.
- New tRPC mutation (mirroring `updateUserDefaultConferencingApp`) or extend `updateProfile` to accept/write this metadata field.
- Settings UI: add a `Select` control to `general-view.tsx` (or a new section) listing allowed landing pages.
- Modify `apps/web/app/page.tsx`: after the onboarding check, read `session.user.metadata?.defaultLandingPage` (or fetch via `UserRepository`) and redirect there instead of the literal `/event-types`, falling back to `/event-types` if unset.

This is a small, well-contained feature — low-moderate effort for a student developer, since it follows an existing established pattern end-to-end.

94	      { ...newSeatedBookingObject, rescheduleUid },
95	      seatedBooking,

104	  if (resultBooking) {
105	    const metadata = {
106	      ...(typeof resultBooking.metadata === "object" && resultBooking.metadata),
107	      ...reqBodyMetadata,
108	    };
109	
110	    const webhookData: EventPayloadType = {
111	      ...evt,
112	      ...eventTypeInfo,
113	      uid: resultBooking?.uid || uid,
114	      bookingId: seatedBooking?.id,
115	      attendeeSeatId: resultBooking?.seatReferenceUid,
116	      rescheduleUid,
117	      rescheduleStartTime: originalRescheduledBooking?.startTime
118	        ? dayjs(originalRescheduledBooking?.startTime).utc().format()
119	        : undefined,
120	      rescheduleEndTime: originalRescheduledBooking?.endTime
121	        ? dayjs(originalRescheduledBooking?.endTime).utc().format()
122	        : undefined,

125	      status: "ACCEPTED",
126	      smsReminderNumber: invitee[0]?.phoneNumber || smsReminderNumber || undefined,
127	      rescheduledBy,
128	    };
129	
130	    await handleWebhookTrigger({ subscriberOptions, eventTrigger, webhookData, isDryRun, traceContext });
131	  }

36	/**
37	 * Atomically adds a seat to a booking with race condition protection.
38	 * Uses a transaction with a fresh read to prevent TOCTOU race conditions
39	 * where concurrent requests could exceed the seat limit.
40	 */
41	export async function addSeatToBooking(input: AddSeatInput, prismaClient: PrismaClient = prisma) {
42	  const referenceUid = uuid();
43	
44	  return prismaClient.$transaction(async (tx) => {
45	    // Lock the booking row with FOR UPDATE to prevent concurrent modifications
46	    // This ensures only one transaction can read and modify seat count at a time
47	    await tx.$queryRaw`SELECT id FROM "Booking" WHERE uid = ${input.bookingUid} FOR UPDATE`;
48	
49	    // Fresh read inside transaction to get the current seat count
50	    const freshBooking = await tx.booking.findUnique({
51	      where: { uid: input.bookingUid },
52	      select: {
53	        attendees: {
54	          select: {
55	            bookingSeat: {
56	              select: { id: true },
57	            },
58	          },
59	        },
60	      },
61	    });
62	
63	    if (!freshBooking) {
64	      throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 404, message: "Booking not found" });
65	    }
66	
67	    // Check seat availability with fresh data
68	    // Only enforce the limit when seatsPerTimeSlot > 0 (matching original behavior
69	    // where falsy seatsPerTimeSlot would skip this check entirely)
70	    const currentSeatCount = freshBooking.attendees.filter((attendee) => !!attendee.bookingSeat).length;
71	    if (input.seatsPerTimeSlot > 0 && input.seatsPerTimeSlot <= currentSeatCount) {
72	      throw new HttpError({
73	        statusCode: 409,
74	        message: ErrorCode.BookingSeatsFull,
75	      });
76	    }
77	
78	    // Create the attendee and seat atomically within the transaction
79	    await tx.booking.update({
80	      where: { uid: input.bookingUid },
81	      data: {
82	        attendees: {
83	          create: {
84	            email: input.attendee.email,

107	      },
108	    });

110	    return await tx.bookingSeat.findUnique({
111	      where: { referenceUid },
112	    });
113	  });

commit 761b780aa2b2cf3f88b60549a34990071972cea9
Author: shafi-VM <adshafi001@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Jul 9 14:23:03 2026 +0530

    fix(bookings): refund all seat payments when cancelling a paid seated… (#29685)
    
    * fix(bookings): refund all seat payments when cancelling a paid seated booking
    
    A paid seated booking creates one Payment row per seat on the same bookingId (each seat's payment_intent.succeeded webhook flips only its own payment via handlePaymentSuccess). processPaymentRefund only refunded payment.find((p) => p.success) — the first successful payment — so fully cancelling a multi-seat paid booking with an auto-refund policy refunded a single seat and left the other attendees charged with no error surfaced.
    
    Refund every successful, not-yet-refunded payment instead.
    
    Tests: unit regression in processPaymentRefund.test.ts (all payments refunded, verified red before the fix); integration test in handleCancelBooking.test.ts proving a full cancel of a seated multi-payment booking hands all payments to the refund path.
    
    * fix(bookings): make seat refunds resilient and drop dayjs in test
    
    Address CodeRabbit review on #29685:
    
    - processPaymentRefund now attempts every seat's refund independently and throws an aggregate error, so one provider failure no longer skips the remaining seats.
    - Add a regression test for that resilience, and use native Date instead of dayjs for fixed-offset test timestamps.

2	import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
3	import { handlePaymentRefund } from "@calcom/features/bookings/lib/payment/handlePaymentRefund";
4	import { RefundPolicy } from "@calcom/lib/payment/types";
5	import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";
6	import type { Payment, Prisma } from "@calcom/prisma/client";
7	import { EventTypeMetaDataSchema } from "@calcom/prisma/zod-utils";
8	
9	export const processPaymentRefund = async ({
10	  booking,
11	  teamId,
12	}: {
13	  booking: {
14	    startTime: Date;
15	    endTime: Date;
16	    payment: Payment[];
17	    eventType: {
18	      owner?: {
19	        id: number;
20	      } | null;
21	      metadata?: Prisma.JsonValue;
22	    } | null;
23	  };
24	  teamId?: number | null;
25	}) => {
26	  const { startTime, eventType, payment } = booking;
27	  if (!teamId && !eventType?.owner) return;
28	
29	  // A paid seated booking creates one Payment per seat on the same bookingId, so refund every
30	  // successful (not-yet-refunded) payment — not just the first — otherwise the other seats stay charged.
31	  const successfulPayments = payment.filter((p) => p.success && !p.refunded);
32	  const [successPayment] = successfulPayments;
33	  if (!successPayment) return;
34	
35	  const eventTypeMetadata = EventTypeMetaDataSchema.parse(eventType?.metadata);
36	  const appData = getPaymentAppData({
37	    currency: successPayment.currency,
38	    metadata: eventTypeMetadata,
39	    price: successPayment.amount,
40	  });
41	
42	  if (!appData?.refundPolicy || appData.refundPolicy === RefundPolicy.NEVER) return;
43	
44	  const credentialWhereClause: Prisma.CredentialFindManyArgs["where"] = {
45	    appId: successPayment.appId,
46	  };
47	  if (eventType?.owner) {
48	    credentialWhereClause.userId = eventType.owner.id;
49	  } else if (teamId) {
50	    credentialWhereClause.teamId = teamId;
51	  }
52	
53	  const paymentAppCredentials = await prisma.credential.findMany({
54	    where: credentialWhereClause,
55	    select: {
56	      key: true,
57	      appId: true,
58	      app: {
59	        select: {
60	          categories: true,
61	          dirName: true,
62	        },
63	      },
64	    },
65	  });
66	
67	  const paymentAppCredential = paymentAppCredentials.find((credential) => {
68	    return credential.appId === successPayment.appId;
69	  });
70	
71	  if (!paymentAppCredential) return;
72	
73	  const { refundPolicy, refundCountCalendarDays, refundDaysCount } = appData;
74	
75	  //refundDaysCount would always be present in case DAYS is selected, but adding it in AND jut for type safety
76	  if (refundPolicy === RefundPolicy.DAYS && refundDaysCount) {
77	    const refundDeadline =
78	      refundCountCalendarDays === true
79	        ? dayjs(startTime).subtract(refundDaysCount, "days")
80	        : // businessDaysSubtract exists on extended dayjs instance, but ts is messing up
81	          // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment
82	          //@ts-ignore
83	          dayjs(startTime).businessDaysSubtract(refundDaysCount);
84	    if (dayjs().isAfter(refundDeadline)) return;
85	  }
86	  // Attempt every refund independently so one provider failure doesn't leave the remaining seats
87	  // charged, then surface an aggregate error for the caller to log/report.
88	  const refundErrors: unknown[] = [];
89	  for (const paymentToRefund of successfulPayments) {
90	    try {
91	      await handlePaymentRefund(paymentToRefund.id, paymentAppCredential);
92	    } catch (error) {
93	      refundErrors.push(error);
94	    }
95	  }
96	
97	  if (refundErrors.length) {
98	    throw new Error(
99	      `Failed to refund ${refundErrors.length} of ${successfulPayments.length} payment(s): ${refundErrors
100	        .map((error) => (error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)))
101	        .join("; ")}`
102	    );
103	  }
104	};

## How Seats Work in cal.diy (cal.com fork)

**1. Data model** (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:1330`): `BookingSeat` is a join/extension table — one `Booking` row is shared by all attendees of a seated slot. Each seat is one `Attendee` row (1:1 with `BookingSeat` via unique `attendeeId`) plus a `BookingSeat` row holding a unique `referenceUid` (the secret token identifying that specific seat/attendee) and `data`/`metadata` JSON (per-seat form responses). So: 1 Booking → many Attendees → each Attendee optionally has 1 BookingSeat with its own `referenceUid`.

**2. Creation** (`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleSeats/`): `handleSeats.ts` finds the existing ACCEPTED booking at that slot/uid, rejects if the same email already holds a seat, then calls `createNewSeat.ts`, which uses `addSeatToBooking()` — a `$transaction` with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` row lock plus a fresh count check against `eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot` to avoid race conditions. If seats are full it throws `HttpError 409 ErrorCode.BookingSeatsFull`. Payment (if any) is per-seat, creating one `Payment` row per attendee on the same `bookingId`.

**3. Viewing**: Organizers see the full attendee roster in the bookings list (`apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx`, with grouped "+N more" and per-attendee no-show toggles) and in the booking detail sheet, which shows only a `slots_taken` count (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookingDetailsSheet.tsx:790-811`) gated by `eventType.seatsShowAttendees`.

**4. Editing/Cancelling** — yes, at both granularities:
- **Individual seat cancel**: an attendee visiting their own booking page with `?seatReferenceUid=...` gets a cancel flow (`apps/web/components/dialog/CancelBookingDialog.tsx` → `CancelBooking.tsx` → `POST /api/cancel` with `seatReferenceUid`) that hits `handleCancelBooking.ts` → `cancelAttendeeSeat.ts`, which deletes just that `Attendee`/`BookingSeat` row, leaving the booking and other seats intact.
- **Whole-booking cancel**: without a `seatReferenceUid`, `handleCancelBooking.ts` requires the caller be the event host/owner (line ~176), then cancels the whole booking and deletes all attendees. `processPaymentRefund.ts` now refunds every successful/unrefunded payment (fixed by commit 761b780a, #29685) rather than just the first.
- **Reschedule**: `handleSeats/reschedule/attendee/attendeeRescheduleSeatedBooking.ts` moves only one seat; `reschedule/owner/ownerRescheduleSeatedBooking.ts` + `moveSeatedBookingToNewTimeSlot.ts`/`combineTwoSeatedBookings.ts` move the whole booking (all seats), merging into an existing slot if one exists.

**UI limitation**: The organizer's dashboard "Cancel" action (`apps/web/components/booking/actions/bookingActions.ts:66-75`) never passes a `seatReferenceUid` — it always cancels the entire booking. There is no dashboard button letting an organizer cancel one specific attendee's seat; only the individual attendee, via their own seat-scoped link, can do that.

- **Whole-booking cancel**: without a `seatReferenceUid`, `handleCancelBooking.ts` requires the caller be the event host/owner (line ~176), then cancels the whole booking and deletes all attendees. `processPaymentRefund.ts` now refunds every successful/unrefunded payment (fixed by commit 761b780a, #29685) rather than just the first.

**UI limitation**: The organizer's dashboard "Cancel" action (`apps/web/components/booking/actions/bookingActions.ts:66-75`) never passes a `seatReferenceUid` — it always cancels the entire booking. _**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 16:54:46Z)**_

Here's how seats (multi-attendee) bookings work in this codebase, and what's actually editable today.

## The mechanism

A seated slot is **one `Booking` row shared by everyone**, not separate bookings per attendee. Each attendee gets:
- An `Attendee` row (their name/email/timezone)
- A `BookingSeat` row linked 1:1 to that attendee, holding a unique `referenceUid` — a private token that identifies *that specific person's* seat and lets them manage it independently.

So: 1 `Booking` → N `Attendee`s → each optionally has 1 `BookingSeat`.

**Creating a seat**: `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleSeats/createNewSeat.ts` locks the row (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) and re-checks the seat count against `eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot` before adding an attendee, to avoid a race where two people grab the last seat simultaneously — if full, it throws a 409 (`BookingSeatsFull`). If the event is paid, each seat gets its own `Payment` row on the same booking.

## Can you view/edit/cancel? Yes, but asymmetrically:

**Viewing** — organizers see the full attendee roster in the bookings list (`BookingListItem.tsx`), with per-attendee no-show toggles. The booking detail sheet only shows a "`N` slots taken" count, and only if the event type has `seatsShowAttendees` enabled.

**Cancelling — this is the asymmetric part:**
- **An individual attendee** can cancel *just their own seat* — their personal booking-confirmation link includes a `seatReferenceUid`, and that flow deletes only their `Attendee`/`BookingSeat` row, leaving everyone else's seat intact.
- **The organizer**, however, has **no way to cancel a single attendee's seat from the dashboard.** The "Cancel" button on the bookings list (`bookingActions.ts:66-75`) never passes a `seatReferenceUid` — it always cancels the *entire* booking, kicking everyone out at once. That's a real gap: an organizer who wants to remove one no-show attendee from a 10-seat webinar can't do it through the UI; only that attendee, using their own private link, can remove themselves.
- When the whole booking is cancelled, a recent fix (commit `761b780a`, PR #29685 — visible in your git log) corrected refund logic to refund **every** seat's payment, not just the first one.

**Rescheduling** works at both levels too: attendees can move just their own seat, or the organizer can move the entire seated slot (merging into another existing slot if one already exists at the new time).

**Bottom line:** individual-seat management exists, but it's attendee-self-service only — there's a genuine missing feature for organizers to remove a single seat-holder without cancelling everyone. Want me to look at what it'd take to add that (an organizer-facing "remove this attendee" action)?

Yes — there's already a working language switcher.

**Where:** Settings → My Account → General (`apps/web/modules/settings/my-account/general-view.tsx`), a "Language" dropdown (`data-testid="locale-select"`) built from `localeOptions` (`packages/lib/i18n.ts`).

**Scope:** 44 languages are supported — `packages/i18n/locales/` has a folder per locale (English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Chinese, Arabic, Portuguese, and many more).

**How it's stored/applied:** it's a real per-user setting — `User.locale` in the Prisma schema (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:431`), persisted via the same profile-update mutation as the rest of that settings page. On save, it also sets a `calNewLocale` cookie client-side so the change takes effect immediately without waiting for a full server round-trip.

So this isn't something that needs building — it already works today. If you want, I can walk through the actual UI flow (log in, go to Settings → My Account, change Language) or dig into how the translation strings themselves get loaded per-locale if you're curious about that mechanism.

60	  return fieldTypesConfigMap[fieldForm.watch("type") || "text"];
61	}
62	
63	const getLocationFieldType = (field: RhfFormField) => {
64	  const baseFieldType = fieldTypesConfigMap[field.type];
65	
66	  if (field.name === "location") {
67	    return { ...baseFieldType, label: "Location" };
68	  }
69	
70	  return baseFieldType;
71	};
72	
73	function isWhitespaceOnly(val: unknown): boolean {
74	  return typeof val === "string" && val.length > 0 && val.trim().length === 0;
75	}
76	
77	function hasWhitespaceOnlyLabel(data: RhfFormField): boolean {
78	  if (isWhitespaceOnly(data.label)) return true;
79	  const variants = data.variantsConfig?.variants;
80	  if (!variants) return false;
81	  for (const variant of Object.values(variants)) {
82	    const fields = variant?.fields ?? [];
83	    for (const f of fields) {
84	      if (isWhitespaceOnly(f?.label)) return true;
85	    }
86	  }
87	  return false;
88	}
