90	/**
91	 * It works with a react-hook-form only.
92	 * `formProp` specifies the name of the property in the react-hook-form that has the fields. This is where fields would be updated.
93	 */
94	export const FormBuilder = function FormBuilder({
95	  title,
96	  description,
97	  addFieldLabel,
98	  formProp,
99	  disabled,
100	  LockedIcon,
101	  dataStore,
102	  shouldConsiderRequired,
103	  showPriceField,
104	  paymentCurrency = "USD",
105	  showPhoneAndEmailToggle = false,
106	}: {
107	  formProp: string;
108	  title: string;
109	  description: string;
110	  addFieldLabel: string;
111	  disabled: boolean;
112	  LockedIcon: false | JSX.Element;
113	  showPhoneAndEmailToggle?: boolean;
114	  /**
115	   * A readonly dataStore that is used to lookup the options for the fields. It works in conjunction with the field.getOptionAt property which acts as the key in options
116	   */
117	  dataStore: DataStore;
118	  /**
119	   * This is kind of a hack to allow certain fields to be just shown as required when they might not be required in a strict sense
120	   * e.g. Location field has a default value at backend so API can send no location but formBuilder in UI doesn't allow it.
121	   */
122	  shouldConsiderRequired?: (field: RhfFormField) => boolean | undefined;
123	  showPriceField?: boolean;
124	  paymentCurrency?: string;
125	}) {
126	  // I would have liked to give Form Builder it's own Form but nested Forms aren't something that browsers support.
127	  // So, this would reuse the same Form as the parent form.
128	  const fieldsForm = useFormContext<RhfForm>();
129	  const [parent] = useAutoAnimate<HTMLUListElement>();
130	  const { t } = useLocale();
131	
132	  const { fields, swap, remove, update, append } = useFieldArray({
133	    control: fieldsForm.control,
134	    // HACK: It allows any property name to be used for instead of `fields` property name
135	    name: formProp as unknown as "fields",
136	  });
137	
138	  const [fieldDialog, setFieldDialog] = useState({
139	    isOpen: false,
140	    fieldIndex: -1,
141	    data: {} as RhfFormField | null,
142	  });
143	
144	  const addField = () => {
145	    setFieldDialog({
146	      isOpen: true,
147	      fieldIndex: -1,
148	      data: null,
149	    });
150	  };
151	
152	  const editField = (index: number, data: RhfFormField) => {
153	    setFieldDialog({
154	      isOpen: true,
155	      fieldIndex: index,
156	      data,
157	    });
158	  };
159	
160	  const removeField = (index: number) => {
161	    remove(index);
162	  };
163	
164	  return (
165	    <div>
166	      <div>
167	        <div className="text-default text-sm font-semibold leading-none ltr:mr-1 rtl:ml-1">
168	          {title}
169	          {LockedIcon}
170	        </div>
171	        <div className="flex items-start justify-between">
172	          <p className="text-subtle mt-1 max-w-[280px] wrap-break-word text-sm sm:max-w-[500px]">
173	            {description}
174	          </p>
175	          {showPhoneAndEmailToggle && (
176	            <ToggleGroup
177	              value={(() => {
178	                const phoneField = fields.find((field) => field.name === "attendeePhoneNumber");
179	                const emailField = fields.find((field) => field.name === "email");
180	
181	                if (phoneField && !phoneField.hidden && phoneField.required && !emailField?.required) {
182	                  return "phone";
183	                }
184	
185	                return "email";
186	              })()}
187	              options={[
188	                {
189	                  value: "email",
190	                  label: "Email",
191	                  iconLeft: <MailIcon className="h-4 w-4" />,
192	                },
193	                {
194	                  value: "phone",
195	                  label: "Phone",
196	                  iconLeft: <PhoneIcon className="h-4 w-4" />,
197	                },
198	              ]}
199	              onValueChange={(value) => {
200	                const phoneFieldIndex = fields.findIndex((field) => field.name === "attendeePhoneNumber");
201	                const emailFieldIndex = fields.findIndex((field) => field.name === "email");
202	                if (value === "email") {
203	                  update(emailFieldIndex, {
204	                    ...fields[emailFieldIndex],
205	                    hidden: false,
206	                    required: true,
207	                  });
208	                  update(phoneFieldIndex, {
209	                    ...fields[phoneFieldIndex],
210	                    hidden: true,
211	                    required: false,
212	                  });
213	                } else if (value === "phone") {
214	                  update(emailFieldIndex, {
215	                    ...fields[emailFieldIndex],
216	                    hidden: true,
217	                    required: false,
218	                  });
219	                  update(phoneFieldIndex, {
220	                    ...fields[phoneFieldIndex],
221	                    hidden: false,
222	                    required: true,
223	                  });
224	                }
225	              }}
226	            />
227	          )}
228	        </div>
229	        <p className="text-default mt-5 text-sm font-semibold leading-none ltr:mr-1 rtl:ml-1">
230	          {t("questions")}
231	        </p>
232	        <p className="text-subtle mt-1 max-w-[280px] wrap-break-word text-sm sm:max-w-[500px]">
233	          {t("all_info_your_booker_provide")}
234	        </p>
235	        <ul ref={parent} className="border-subtle divide-subtle mt-4 divide-y rounded-md border">
236	          {fields.map((field, index) => {
237	            let options = field.options ?? null;
238	            const sources = [...(field.sources || [])];
239	            const isRequired = shouldConsiderRequired ? shouldConsiderRequired(field) : field.required;
240	            if (!options && field.getOptionsAt) {
241	              const {
242	                source: { label: sourceLabel },
243	                value,
244	              } = dataStore.options[field.getOptionsAt as keyof typeof dataStore] ?? [];
245	              options = value;
246	              options.forEach((option) => {
247	                sources.push({
248	                  id: option.value,
249	                  label: sourceLabel,
250	                  type: "system",
251	                });
252	              });
253	            }
254	
255	            if (fieldsThatSupportLabelAsSafeHtml.includes(field.type)) {
256	              field = { ...field, labelAsSafeHtml: markdownToSafeHTMLClient(field.label ?? "") };
257	            }
258	            const numOptions = options?.length ?? 0;
259	            const firstOptionInput =
260	              field.optionsInputs?.[options?.[0]?.value as keyof typeof field.optionsInputs];
261	            const doesFirstOptionHaveInput = !!firstOptionInput;
262	            // If there is only one option and it doesn't have an input required, we don't show the Field for it.
263	            // Because booker doesn't see this in UI, there is no point showing it in FormBuilder to configure it.
264	            if (field.hideWhenJustOneOption && numOptions <= 1 && !doesFirstOptionHaveInput) {
265	              return null;
266	            }
267	
268	            const fieldType = getLocationFieldType(field);
269	            const isFieldEditableSystemButOptional = field.editable === "system-but-optional";
270	            const isFieldEditableSystemButHidden = field.editable === "system-but-hidden";
271	            const isFieldEditableSystem = field.editable === "system";
272	            const isUserField =
273	              !isFieldEditableSystem && !isFieldEditableSystemButOptional && !isFieldEditableSystemButHidden;
274	
275	            if (!fieldType) {
276	              throw new Error(`Invalid field type - ${field.type}`);
277	            }
278	            const groupedBySourceLabel = sources.reduce(
279	              (groupBy, source) => {
280	                const item = groupBy[source.label] || [];
281	                if (source.type === "user" || source.type === "default") {
282	                  return groupBy;
283	                }
284	                item.push(source);
285	                groupBy[source.label] = item;
286	                return groupBy;
287	              },
288	              {} as Record<string, NonNullable<(typeof field)["sources"]>>
289	            );
290	
291	            return (
292	              <li
293	                key={field.name}
294	                data-testid={`field-${field.name}`}
295	                className="hover:bg-cal-muted group relative flex items-center justify-between p-4 transition">
296	                {!disabled && (
297	                  <>
298	                    {index >= 1 && (
299	                      <button
300	                        type="button"
301	                        className="bg-default text-muted hover:text-emphasis disabled:hover:text-muted border-subtle hover:border-emphasis invisible absolute -left-[12px] -ml-4 -mt-4 mb-4 hidden h-6 w-6 scale-0 items-center justify-center rounded-md border p-1 transition-all hover:shadow disabled:hover:border-inherit disabled:hover:shadow-none group-hover:visible group-hover:scale-100 sm:ml-0 sm:flex"
302	                        onClick={() => swap(index, index - 1)}>
303	                        <ArrowUpIcon className="h-5 w-5" />
304	                      </button>
305	                    )}
306	                    {index < fields.length - 1 && (
307	                      <button
308	                        type="button"
309	                        className="bg-default text-muted hover:border-emphasis border-subtle hover:text-emphasis disabled:hover:text-muted invisible absolute -left-[12px] -ml-4 mt-8 hidden h-6 w-6 scale-0 items-center justify-center rounded-md border p-1 transition-all hover:shadow disabled:hover:border-inherit disabled:hover:shadow-none group-hover:visible group-hover:scale-100 sm:ml-0 sm:flex"
310	                        onClick={() => swap(index, index + 1)}>
311	                        <ArrowDownIcon className="h-5 w-5" />
312	                      </button>
313	                    )}
314	                  </>
315	                )}
316	                <div>
317	                  <div className="mr-4 flex flex-col lg:flex-row lg:items-center">
318	                    <div className="text-default text-sm font-semibold ltr:mr-2 rtl:ml-2">
319	                      <FieldLabel field={field} />
320	                    </div>
321	                    <div className="flex items-center space-x-2">
322	                      {field.hidden ? (
323	                        // Hidden field can't be required, so we don't need to show the Optional badge
324	                        <Badge variant="grayWithoutHover">{t("hidden")}</Badge>
325	                      ) : (
326	                        <Badge variant="grayWithoutHover" data-testid={isRequired ? "required" : "optional"}>
327	                          {isRequired ? t("required") : t("optional")}
328	                        </Badge>
329	                      )}
330	                      {Object.entries(groupedBySourceLabel).map(([sourceLabel, sources], key) => (
331	                        // We don't know how to pluralize `sourceLabel` because it can be anything
332	                        <Badge key={key} variant="blue">
333	                          {sources.length} {sources.length === 1 ? sourceLabel : `${sourceLabel}s`}
334	                        </Badge>
335	                      ))}
336	                    </div>
337	                  </div>
338	                  <p className="text-subtle max-w-[280px] wrap-break-word pt-1 text-sm sm:max-w-[500px]">
339	                    {fieldType.label}
340	                  </p>
341	                </div>
342	                {field.editable !== "user-readonly" && !disabled && (
343	                  <div className="flex items-center space-x-2">
344	                    {!isFieldEditableSystem && !isFieldEditableSystemButHidden && !disabled && (
345	                      <Switch
346	                        data-testid="toggle-field"
347	                        disabled={isFieldEditableSystem}
348	                        checked={!field.hidden}
349	                        onCheckedChange={(checked) => {
350	                          update(index, { ...field, hidden: !checked });
351	                        }}
352	                        tooltip={t("show_on_booking_page")}
353	                      />
354	                    )}
355	                    {isUserField && (
356	                      <Button
357	                        data-testid="delete-field-action"
358	                        color="destructive"
359	                        disabled={!isUserField}
360	                        variant="icon"
361	                        onClick={() => {
362	                          removeField(index);
363	                        }}
364	                        StartIcon="trash-2"
365	                      />
366	                    )}
367	                    <Button
368	                      data-testid="edit-field-action"
369	                      color="secondary"
370	                      onClick={() => {
371	                        editField(index, field);
372	                      }}>
373	                      {t("edit")}
374	                    </Button>
375	                  </div>
376	                )}
377	              </li>
378	            );
379	          })}
380	        </ul>
381	        {!disabled && (
382	          <Button
383	            color="minimal"
384	            data-testid="add-field"
385	            onClick={addField}
386	            className="mt-4"
387	            StartIcon="plus">
388	            {addFieldLabel}
389	          </Button>
390	        )}
391	      </div>
392	      {/* Move this Dialog in another component and it would take with it fieldForm */}
393	      {fieldDialog.isOpen && (
394	        <FieldEditDialog
395	          dialog={fieldDialog}
396	          onOpenChange={(isOpen) =>
397	            setFieldDialog({
398	              isOpen,
399	              fieldIndex: -1,
400	              data: null,
401	            })
402	          }
403	          handleSubmit={(data: Parameters<SubmitHandler<RhfFormField>>[0]) => {
404	            const type = data.type || "text";
405	            const isNewField = !fieldDialog.data;
406	
407	            if (hasWhitespaceOnlyLabel(data)) {
408	              showToast(t("label_cannot_be_whitespace"), "error");
409	              return;
410	            }
411	
412	            if (data.name === "guests" && type !== "multiemail") {
413	              showToast(t("guests_field_must_be_multiemail"), "error");
414	              return;
415	            }
416	
417	            if (isNewField && fields.some((f) => f.name === data.name)) {
418	              showToast(t("form_builder_field_already_exists"), "error");
419	              return;
420	            }
421	            if (fieldDialog.data) {
422	              update(fieldDialog.fieldIndex, data);
423	            } else {
424	              const field: RhfFormField = {
425	                ...data,
426	                type,
427	                sources: [
428	                  {
429	                    label: "User",
430	                    type: "user",
431	                    id: "user",
432	                    fieldRequired: data.required,
433	                  },
434	                ],
435	              };
436	              field.editable = field.editable || "user";
437	              append(field);
438	            }
439	            setFieldDialog({
440	              isOpen: false,
441	              fieldIndex: -1,
442	              data: null,
443	            });
444	          }}
445	          shouldConsiderRequired={shouldConsiderRequired}
446	          showPriceField={showPriceField}
447	          paymentCurrency={paymentCurrency}
448	        />
449	      )}
450	    </div>
451	  );
452	};
453	
454	function Options({
455	  label = "Options",
456	  value,
457	
458	  onChange = () => { },
459	  className = "",
460	  readOnly = false,
461	  showPrice = false,
462	  paymentCurrency,
463	}: {
464	  label?: string;
465	  value: { label: string; value: string; price?: number }[];
466	  onChange?: (value: { label: string; value: string; price?: number }[]) => void;
467	  className?: string;
468	  readOnly?: boolean;
469	  showPrice?: boolean;
470	  paymentCurrency: string;
471	}) {
472	  const { t } = useLocale();
473	
474	  const [animationRef] = useAutoAnimate<HTMLUListElement>();
475	  if (!value) {
476	    onChange([
477	      {
478	        label: "Option 1",
479	        value: "Option 1",
480	      },
481	      {
482	        label: "Option 2",
483	        value: "Option 2",
484	      },
485	    ]);
486	  }
487	  return (
488	    <div className={className}>
489	      <Label>{label}</Label>
490	      <div className="bg-cal-muted rounded-md p-4" data-testid="options-container">
491	        <ul ref={animationRef} className="flex flex-col gap-3">
492	          {value?.map((option, index) => (
493	            <li key={index}>
494	              <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
495	                <div className="relative grow">
496	                  <Input
497	                    required
498	                    value={option.label}
499	                    onChange={(e) => {
500	                      // Right now we use label of the option as the value of the option. It allows use to not separately lookup the optionId to know the optionValue
501	                      // It has the same drawback that if the label is changed, the value of the option will change. It is not a big deal for now.
502	                      const newOptions = [...(value || [])];
503	                      newOptions.splice(index, 1, {
504	                        label: e.target.value,
505	                        value: e.target.value.trim(),
506	                      });
507	                      onChange(newOptions);
508	                    }}
509	                    readOnly={readOnly}
510	                    placeholder={t("enter_option", { index: index + 1 })}
511	                    className={value.length > 2 && !readOnly ? "pr-8" : ""}
512	                  />
513	                  {value.length > 2 && !readOnly && (
514	                    <Button
515	                      type="button"
516	                      className="absolute right-1 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 hover:bg-transparent! focus:bg-transparent! focus:outline-none! focus:ring-0!"
517	                      size="sm"
518	                      color="minimal"
519	                      StartIcon="x"
520	                      onClick={() => {
521	                        if (!value) return;
522	                        const newOptions = [...(value || [])];
523	                        newOptions.splice(index, 1);
524	                        onChange(newOptions);
525	                      }}
526	                    />
527	                  )}
528	                </div>
529	                {showPrice && (
530	                  <div className="w-24">
531	                    <InputField
532	                      type="number"
533	                      min={0}
534	                      step="0.01"
535	                      value={option.price}
536	                      onChange={(e) => {
537	                        const val = e.target.value;
538	                        const numValue = val === "" ? undefined : Number(val);
539	                        const updatedOptions = [...(value || [])];
540	                        updatedOptions[index] = {
541	                          ...option,
542	                          price: numValue,
543	                        };
544	                        onChange(updatedOptions);
545	                      }}
546	                      readOnly={readOnly}
547	                      placeholder="0"
548	                      addOnLeading={getCurrencySymbol(paymentCurrency)}
549	                    />
550	                  </div>
551	                )}
552	              </div>
553	            </li>
554	          ))}
555	        </ul>
556	        {!readOnly && (
557	          <Button
558	            color="minimal"
559	            data-testid="add-option"
560	            className="mt-3"
561	            onClick={() => {
562	              const newOptions = [...(value || [])];
563	              newOptions.push({ label: "", value: "", price: 0 });
564	              onChange(newOptions);
565	            }}
566	            StartIcon="plus">
567	            Add an Option
568	          </Button>
569	        )}
570	      </div>
571	    </div>
572	  );
573	}
574	
575	const CheckboxFieldLabel = ({ fieldForm }: { fieldForm: UseFormReturn<RhfFormField> }) => {
576	  const { t } = useLocale();
577	  const [firstRender, setFirstRender] = useState(true);
578	  return (
579	    <div className="mt-6">
580	      <Label>{t("label")}</Label>
581	      <Editor
582	        getText={() => md.render(fieldForm.getValues("label") || "")}
583	        setText={(value: string) => {
584	          fieldForm.setValue("label", turndown(value), { shouldDirty: true });
585	        }}
586	        excludedToolbarItems={["blockType", "bold", "italic"]}
587	        disableLists
588	        firstRender={firstRender}
589	        setFirstRender={setFirstRender}
590	        placeholder={t(fieldForm.getValues("defaultLabel") || "")}
591	      />
592	    </div>
593	  );
594	};
595	
596	function FieldEditDialog({
597	  dialog,
598	  onOpenChange,
599	  handleSubmit,
600	  shouldConsiderRequired,
601	  showPriceField,
602	  paymentCurrency,
603	}: {
604	  dialog: { isOpen: boolean; fieldIndex: number; data: RhfFormField | null };
605	  onOpenChange: (isOpen: boolean) => void;
606	  handleSubmit: SubmitHandler<RhfFormField>;
607	  shouldConsiderRequired?: (field: RhfFormField) => boolean | undefined;
608	  showPriceField?: boolean;
609	  paymentCurrency: string;
610	}) {
611	  const { t } = useLocale();
612	  const isPlatform = useIsPlatform();
613	  const fieldForm = useForm<RhfFormField>({
614	    defaultValues: dialog.data || {},
615	    //resolver: zodResolver(fieldSchema),
616	  });
617	  const formFieldType = fieldForm.getValues("type");
618	
619	  useEffect(() => {
620	    if (!formFieldType) {
621	      return;
622	    }
623	
624	    const variantsConfig = getVariantsConfig({
625	      type: formFieldType,
626	      variantsConfig: fieldForm.getValues("variantsConfig"),
627	    });
628	
629	    // We need to set the variantsConfig in the RHF instead of using a derived value because RHF won't have the variantConfig for the variant that's not rendered yet.
630	    fieldForm.setValue("variantsConfig", variantsConfig);
631	  }, [fieldForm]);
632	
633	  const isFieldEditMode = !!dialog.data;
634	  const fieldType = getCurrentFieldType(fieldForm);
635	
636	  const variantsConfig = fieldForm.watch("variantsConfig");
637	
638	  const fieldTypes = Object.values(fieldTypesConfigMap);
639	
640	  return (
641	    <Dialog open={dialog.isOpen} onOpenChange={onOpenChange} modal={false}>
642	      <DialogContent className="max-h-none" data-testid="edit-field-dialog" forceOverlayWhenNoModal={true}>
643	        <Form id="form-builder" form={fieldForm} handleSubmit={handleSubmit}>
644	          <div className="h-auto max-h-[85vh]">
645	            <DialogHeader
646	              title={t("add_a_booking_question")}
647	              subtitle={
648	                <LearnMoreLink
649	                  t={t}
650	                  i18nKey="booking_questions_description"
651	                  href="https://cal.com/help/event-types/booking-questions"
652	                />
653	              }
654	            />
655	            <SelectField
656	              defaultValue={fieldTypesConfigMap.text}
657	              data-testid="test-field-type"
658	              id="test-field-type"
659	              isDisabled={
660	                fieldForm.getValues("editable") === "system" ||
661	                fieldForm.getValues("editable") === "system-but-optional"
662	              }
663	              onChange={(e) => {
664	                const value = e?.value;
665	                if (!value) {
666	                  return;
667	                }
668	                fieldForm.setValue("type", value, { shouldDirty: true });
669	              }}
670	              value={fieldTypesConfigMap[formFieldType]}
671	              options={fieldTypes.filter((f) => !f.systemOnly)}
672	              label={t("input_type")}
673	            />
674	            {(() => {
675	              if (!variantsConfig) {
676	                return (
677	                  <>
678	                    <InputField
679	                      required
680	                      {...fieldForm.register("name")}
681	                      containerClassName="mt-6"
682	                      onChange={(e) => {
683	                        fieldForm.setValue("name", getFieldIdentifier(e.target.value || ""), {
684	                          shouldDirty: true,
685	                        });
686	                      }}
687	                      disabled={
688	                        fieldForm.getValues("editable") === "system" ||
689	                        fieldForm.getValues("editable") === "system-but-optional"
690	                      }
691	                      label={t("identifier")}
692	                    />
693	                    <CheckboxField
694	                      description={t("disable_input_if_prefilled")}
695	                      {...fieldForm.register("disableOnPrefill", { setValueAs: Boolean })}
696	                    />
697	                    <div>
698	                      {formFieldType === "boolean" && !isPlatform ? (
699	                        <CheckboxFieldLabel fieldForm={fieldForm} />
700	                      ) : (
701	                        <InputField
702	                          {...fieldForm.register("label")}
703	                          // System fields have a defaultLabel, so there a label is not required
704	                          required={
705	                            !["system", "system-but-optional"].includes(fieldForm.getValues("editable") || "")
706	                          }
707	                          placeholder={t(fieldForm.getValues("defaultLabel") || "")}
708	                          containerClassName="mt-6"

849	function FieldWithLengthCheckSupport({

897	          // Ensure that minLength field adjusts its restrictions
898	          fieldForm.trigger("minLength");
899	        }}
900	        min={fieldForm.getValues("minLength") || 0}
901	        max={maxAllowedMaxLength}
902	      />
903	    </div>
904	  );

922	        <span

937	    );

940	  const firstField = variantData?.fields?.[0];
941	  const label = firstField?.label?.trim() ? firstField.label : "";
942	  const firstFieldName = firstField?.name;
943	  const defaultLabelFromTypeConfig =
944	    fieldTypeConfigVariants?.[variant as keyof typeof fieldTypeConfigVariants]?.fieldsMap?.[
945	      firstFieldName as keyof (typeof fieldTypeConfigVariants)[typeof variant]["fieldsMap"]
946	    ]?.defaultLabel || "";
947	  return <span>{t(label || defaultLabelFromTypeConfig)}</span>;

955	function VariantFields({
956	  fieldForm,
957	  variantsConfig,
958	}: {
959	  fieldForm: UseFormReturn<RhfFormField>;
960	  variantsConfig: RhfFormField["variantsConfig"];
961	}) {
962	  const { t } = useLocale();
963	  if (!variantsConfig) {
964	    throw new Error("VariantFields component needs variantsConfig");
965	  }
966	  const fieldTypeConfigVariantsConfig = fieldTypesConfigMap[fieldForm.getValues("type")]?.variantsConfig;
967	
968	  if (!fieldTypeConfigVariantsConfig) {
969	    throw new Error("Configuration Issue: FieldType doesn't have `variantsConfig`");
970	  }
971	
972	  const variantToggleLabel = t(fieldTypeConfigVariantsConfig.toggleLabel || "");
973	
974	  const defaultVariant = fieldTypeConfigVariantsConfig.defaultVariant;
975	
976	  const variantNames = Object.keys(variantsConfig.variants);
977	  const otherVariants = variantNames.filter((v) => v !== defaultVariant);
978	  if (otherVariants.length > 1 && variantToggleLabel) {
979	    throw new Error("More than one other variant. Remove toggleLabel ");
980	  }
981	  const otherVariant = otherVariants[0];
982	  const variantName = fieldForm.watch("variant") || defaultVariant;
983	  const variantFields = variantsConfig.variants[variantName as keyof typeof variantsConfig].fields;
984	  /**
985	   * A variant that has just one field can be shown in a simpler way in UI.

987	  const isSimpleVariant = variantFields.length === 1;

1013	          fieldForm.getValues("editable") === "system-but-optional"
1014	        }
1015	        label={t("identifier")}
1016	      />
1017	
1018	      <div className="mt-2">
1019	        <CheckboxField
1020	          description={t("disable_input_if_prefilled")}
1021	          {...fieldForm.register("disableOnPrefill", { setValueAs: Boolean })}
1022	        />
1023	      </div>
1024	
1025	      <ul
1026	        className={classNames(
1027	          !isSimpleVariant ? "border-subtle divide-subtle mt-2 divide-y rounded-md border" : ""
1028	        )}>
1029	        {variantFields.map((f, index) => {
1030	          const rhfVariantFieldPrefix = `variantsConfig.variants.${variantName}.fields.${index}` as const;
1031	          const fieldTypeConfigVariants =
1032	            fieldTypeConfigVariantsConfig.variants[
1033	            variantName as keyof typeof fieldTypeConfigVariantsConfig.variants
1034	            ];
1035	          const appUiFieldConfig =
1036	            fieldTypeConfigVariants.fieldsMap[f.name as keyof typeof fieldTypeConfigVariants.fieldsMap];
1037	
1038	          return (
1039	            <li className={classNames(!isSimpleVariant ? "p-4" : "")} key={f.name}>
1040	              {!isSimpleVariant && (

1042	                  <span>{`Field ${index + 1}`}</span>
1043	                  <span className="text-muted">{t(appUiFieldConfig?.defaultLabel || "")}</span>
1044	                </Label>
1045	              )}
1046	              <InputField
1047	                {...fieldForm.register(`${rhfVariantFieldPrefix}.label`)}
1048	                value={f.label || ""}
1049	                placeholder={t(appUiFieldConfig?.defaultLabel || "")}
1050	                containerClassName="mt-6"
1051	                label={t("label")}
1052	              />
1053	              <InputField
1054	                {...fieldForm.register(`${rhfVariantFieldPrefix}.placeholder`)}
1055	                key={f.name}
1056	                value={f.placeholder || ""}
1057	                containerClassName="mt-6"
1058	                label={t("placeholder")}
1059	                placeholder={t(appUiFieldConfig?.defaultPlaceholder || "")}
1060	              />
1061	
1062	              <div className="mt-6">
1063	                <Controller

## How "Booking Questions" Works

**1. Organizer-side editing** — `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/advanced/FormBuilder.tsx` is a React-hook-form-driven component (uses `useFieldArray` on a `fields` array) rendered inside `EventAdvancedTab.tsx` (imported at line 65, rendered ~line 644) — i.e. the event type's "Advanced" tab. Each field row shows label/type/required badge, with add/edit/delete/reorder (up/down arrow) controls and a `FieldEditDialog` for configuring name, label, placeholder, options, length limits, price, and required/hidden state.

Data model: `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` line 194 — `EventType.bookingFields Json?`. Shape validated by `fieldSchema` in `packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts` (~line 954-1090): `{ name, type, label, defaultLabel, placeholder, required, options[], getOptionsAt, optionsInputs, minLength/maxLength, hidden, editable ("system"|"system-but-optional"|"system-but-hidden"|"user"|"user-readonly"), sources[], variantsConfig, price }`.

**2. Shared form-builder package** — `packages/features/form-builder/`: `fieldTypes.ts` defines `fieldTypesConfigMap`, the single source of truth for the field-type list (`name, email, phone, address, text, number, textarea, select, multiselect, multiemail, radioInput, checkbox, radio, boolean, url`) with per-type capabilities (`needsOptions`, `isTextType`, `supportsLengthCheck`, `supportsPricing`, `variantsConfig` for name splitting). `schema.ts` defines `fieldsSchema`/`fieldTypeConfigSchema` plus `fieldTypesSchemaMap`, which holds per-type `preprocess`/`superRefine` logic reused for validation. `widgets.tsx` renders the actual inputs — reused by both the editor's `FieldEditDialog` and (via a wrapper) the booker.

**3. Attendee-facing side** — `apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookEventForm/BookingFields.tsx` receives the event's `fields` (from `bookingFields`, resolved via `getPublicEvent.ts`/`getBookingFieldsWithSystemFields` in `packages/features/bookings/lib/getBookingFields.ts`) and maps each into `FormBuilderField` (`apps/web/modules/form-builder/components/FormBuilderField.tsx`), driven by `fieldTypesConfigMap` for widget selection.

**4. Validation/storage** — `packages/features/bookings/lib/getBookingResponsesSchema.ts` builds a Zod schema per field using `fieldTypesSchemaMap` (preprocess + superRefine per type). Submitted answers are stored in `Booking.responses Json?` (schema.prisma ~line 868).

**5. Defaults vs custom** — `ensureBookingInputsHaveSystemFields` always injects `name`, `email`, `attendeePhoneNumber`, `location`, guests, notes as system fields (locked/`editable: "system*"`); organizers freely add/reorder/require "user" fields. No conditional-display ("show if X answered Y") logic was found — only `radioInput`'s `optionsInputs` shows a follow-up input based on the selected option (e.g. location type).

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 17:39:39Z)**_

Here's how the "booking questions" feature works — the custom form fields organizers add to their event booking page (email, phone, text, select, etc.).

## The data model

`EventType.bookingFields` is a JSON column (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma`) — an array of field definitions, each with `{ name, type, label, required, options, editable, ... }`. `editable` distinguishes built-in fields (`"system"`, locked) from organizer-added ones (`"user"`, fully editable).

**Defaults that always exist**, injected automatically regardless of what the organizer configures: name, email, phone, location, guests, notes. Organizers can only add/reorder/require *additional* fields on top of these.

## Where organizers configure it

`apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/advanced/FormBuilder.tsx`, rendered inside the event type's **Advanced tab**. It's a react-hook-form field array with add/edit/delete/reorder controls, and a dialog (`FieldEditDialog`) for setting each field's label, placeholder, options, required/hidden state, and (for paid add-ons) price.

## The shared single source of truth

`packages/features/form-builder/fieldTypes.ts` defines every available field type (text, email, phone, address, number, textarea, select, multiselect, multiemail, checkbox, radio, boolean, url, etc.) and what each supports (needs options? supports a price? supports min/max length?). Both the organizer's editor *and* the attendee's booking form read from this same map, so there's no risk of the two sides drifting apart.

## Attendee-facing side

When someone goes to book, `apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookEventForm/BookingFields.tsx` reads the event's `bookingFields`, and for each one renders the matching widget via `FormBuilderField.tsx` — same widget code the organizer sees in the editor preview.

## Validation and storage

`packages/features/bookings/lib/getBookingResponsesSchema.ts` turns those field definitions into a Zod schema (per-type validation logic lives in `fieldTypesSchemaMap`), which validates what the attendee submits. Answers land in `Booking.responses`, another JSON column.

## One limitation worth knowing

There's no general conditional-display logic (e.g., "only show this question if they answered X on a previous one") — the only case close to that is the location-type field's `optionsInputs`, which shows a follow-up input based on which location option was picked.

Want me to walk through actually adding a custom booking question in the running app, or look at a specific piece of this in more depth (e.g., how the price/paid-add-on fields tie into Stripe)?

Sort of — but not in the way you'd expect. There's an app-store entry literally called **"Notion Calendar"** (`packages/app-store/cron/`, slug `cron` — Notion Calendar's original name/domain was Cron), but it's not a real integration:

```json
"__template": "link-as-an-app",
"isOAuth": false,
"dependencies": ["google-calendar"],
"externalLink": { "url": "https://cron.com", "newTab": true }
```

- **No actual code** — the folder only has `config.json` and marketing screenshots, no `.ts`/`.tsx` files at all.
- **`"link-as-an-app"` template** means clicking "Install" in cal.com's App Store just opens `cron.com` in a new tab — it's a promotional listing, not a real calendar sync.
- **`isOAuth: false`** — no API connection is ever made between cal.diy and Notion Calendar.
- The `"dependencies": ["google-calendar"]` hints at the real story: Notion Calendar is itself just a calendar *client* that displays your Google Calendar (or other calendars) — so the actual sync path is **cal.diy ↔ Google Calendar** (a real, fully-implemented integration elsewhere in `app-store/`), and separately, Notion Calendar reads from that same Google Calendar on its own.

**Bottom line:** there's no direct cal.diy ↔ Notion Calendar connection. If someone wants their cal.diy bookings to show up in Notion Calendar, the actual path is: connect **Google Calendar** to cal.diy (real two-way sync, `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/`), and separately add that same Google account to Notion Calendar — the two apps end up in sync *via* Google Calendar, not directly with each other.

Low — essentially not feasible as a direct integration, and here's why.

Looking at how the other real calendar integrations in this codebase work (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/`, `office365calendar/`, generic `caldav-calendar/`), they all sync against a genuine calendar API — Google Calendar API, Microsoft Graph, or the CalDAV protocol. A real Notion Calendar integration would need the same: an API surface to authenticate against and read/write events.

**Notion Calendar doesn't have one.** Per current sources: Notion Calendar isn't backed by its own API — it's purely a *client* app that connects to Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook, or Apple iCloud accounts. The general-purpose Notion REST API (for pages/databases) is unrelated to Notion Calendar's scheduling data; it can't read or write calendar events.

**What that means concretely:**
- There's no OAuth app to register, no calendar-events endpoint to call, no CalDAV server to point at — nothing to build the integration *against*.
- This matches what we found in the codebase: the existing "Notion Calendar" app-store entry is just a `link-as-an-app` marketing listing that opens `cron.com` in a new tab — not a stub for a real integration waiting to be filled in. That's not a corner someone cut; it's the only thing that *could* be built, given Notion Calendar has no API.

**Verdict:** you can't build a direct cal.diy ↔ Notion Calendar sync. The only real path to "get cal.diy bookings into Notion Calendar" is the indirect one already available today — connect **Google Calendar** (or Outlook/iCloud) to cal.diy using the existing real integrations, since that's the same account Notion Calendar is already reading from. If you want, I can walk through how that Google Calendar sync path actually works end-to-end.

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 17:47:39Z)**_

## Answer: No — that exact pattern is not supported

**Direct answer:** You cannot configure a single recurring series to fire on Mon/Wed/Fri (multiple distinct weekdays) with an "ends June 1st"-style end date. The system only supports a uniform frequency + interval + occurrence-count, applied to whatever single date/time the *attendee* picks when booking — not the organizer.

**1. Data model** — `packages/prisma/schema.prisma:214`: `EventType.recurringEvent Json?`. Validated by `recurringEventType` in `packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts:234-243`:
```ts
{ dtstart?: Date, interval: number, count: number, freq: Frequency (nativeEnum), until?: Date, tzid?: string }
```
It's explicly modeled after `RRule.Options` (rrule.js). There's no `byweekday`/`BYDAY` field at all, so multi-weekday patterns are structurally impossible. `until` exists in the zod type but is never populated/exposed anywhere (see below) — count is what actually gets used.

**2. Organizer UI** — `packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/recurring/RecurringEventController.tsx` (rendered via `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/recurring/EventRecurringWebWrapper.tsx` → `EventRecurringTab`). The organizer only sees:
- A toggle to enable recurring
- "Repeats every [N]" — a number input for `interval`
- A frequency `Select` limited to **Yearly / Monthly / Weekly only** (filtered `Number(value) < 3`, excluding Daily and finer)
- "for a maximum of [N] events" — a `count` number input (max 24)

No day-of-week picker, no end-date picker exists in this UI. Default when enabling: `{ interval: 1, count: 12, freq: WEEKLY }`.

**3. Booking-time behavior** — The attendee picks exactly one slot. `packages/lib/parse-dates.ts` (`parseRecurringDates`) builds an `RRule` using that single picked slot as `dtstart`, plus the event type's `freq`/`interval`, expanding it to `recurringCount` future dates via `rule.all()` — always same weekday/time, no way to mix weekdays. `packages/features/bookings/lib/client/booking-event-form/booking-to-mutation-input-mapper.tsx` (`mapRecurringBookingToMutationInput`) turns that expanded date array into N separate booking payloads sharing one generated `recurringEventId`, which `RecurringBookingService.ts` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RecurringBookingService.ts`) submits as individual `Booking` rows (each linked via `recurringEventId`, see `schema.prisma:889/2787`).

**4. End condition** — Only occurrence-`count` is functional (booker/org both cap at a number of events, UI max 24). No functional "ends on date X" — `until` is defined in the zod schema but unused/unwired in both the organizer UI and the booking-generation code.

**What IS supported for your example:** organizer sets Weekly, interval 1, count ~4 (≈"next month"); attendee books, say, Monday 12pm, and gets 4 consecutive Monday-12pm bookings. Wed/Fri instances would need to be separate, independently-booked event types/series.

**Direct answer:** You cannot configure a single recurring series to fire on Mon/Wed/Fri (multiple distinct weekdays) with an "ends June 1st"-style end date. The system only supports a uniform frequency + interval + occurrence-count, applied to whatever single date/time the *attendee* picks when booking — not the organizer.

**1. Data model** — `packages/prisma/schema.prisma:214`: `EventType.recurringEvent Json?`. Validated by `recurringEventType` in `packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts:234-243`:
```ts
{ dtstart?: Date, interval: number, count: number, freq: Frequency (nativeEnum), until?: Date, tzid?: string }
```
It's explicly modeled after `RRule.Options` (rrule.js). There's no `byweekday`/`BYDAY` field at all, so multi-weekday patterns are structurally impossible. `until` exists in the zod type but is never populated/exposed anywhere (see below) — count is what actually gets used.

**2. Organizer UI** — `packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/recurring/RecurringEventController.tsx` (rendered via `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/recurring/EventRecurringWebWrapper.tsx` → `EventRecurringTab`). The organizer only sees:
- A toggle to enable recurring
- "Repeats every [N]" — a number input for `interval`
- A frequency `Select` limited to **Yearly / Monthly / Weekly only** (filtered `Number(value) &lt; 3`, excluding Daily and finer)
- "for a maximum of [N] events" — a `count` number input (max 24)

No day-of-week picker, no end-date picker exists in this UI. Default when enabling: `{ interval: 1, count: 12, freq: WEEKLY }`.

**3. Booking-time behavior** — The attendee picks exactly one slot. `packages/lib/parse-dates.ts` (`parseRecurringDates`) builds an `RRule` using that single picked slot as `dtstart`, plus the event type's `freq`/`interval`, expanding it to `recurringCount` future dates via `rule.all()` — always same weekday/time, no way to mix weekdays. `packages/features/bookings/lib/client/booking-event-form/booking-to-mutation-input-mapper.tsx` (`mapRecurringBookingToMutationInput`) turns that expanded date array into N separate booking payloads sharing one generated `recurringEventId`, which `RecurringBookingService.ts` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RecurringBookingService.ts`) submits as individual `Booking` rows (each linked via `recurringEventId`, see `schema.prisma:889/2787`).

**4. End condition** — Only occurrence-`count` is functional (booker/org both cap at a number of events, UI max 24). No functional "ends on date X" — `until` is defined in the zod schema but unused/unwired in both the organizer UI and the booking-generation code.

**What IS supported for your example:** organizer sets Weekly, interval 1, count ~4 (≈"next month"); attendee books, say, Monday 12pm, and gets 4 consecutive Monday-12pm bookings. Wed/Fri instances would need to be separate, independently-booked event types/series.</result>

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 17:47:51Z)**_

Short answer: **no**, not exactly like that. The system doesn't support a single series firing on multiple specific weekdays (Mon/Wed/Fri) with an end-by-date — it's simpler and structured differently than a typical calendar recurrence.

## How it actually works

**Who picks the recurrence pattern:** The *organizer* configures the recurrence rule on the event type, but the *attendee* picks the single starting slot when they book — the organizer never picks a specific day/time.

**What the organizer can configure** (Recurring tab on the event type):
- **Frequency**: Weekly, Monthly, or Yearly only (no Daily, and definitely no "pick multiple weekdays")
- **Interval**: "Repeats every [N]" — e.g. every 1 week, every 2 weeks
- **Count**: "for a maximum of [N] events" — capped at 24

**What happens at booking time:** the attendee picks one slot — say, Monday at 12pm — and the system generates that many future occurrences (using the `rrule.js` library under the hood) at the *same* weekday/time, spaced by the interval. So "weekly, count 4" starting from a Monday booking gives you 4 consecutive Monday-12pm bookings.

**No end-by-date support**: the underlying schema (`packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts`) technically has an `until` field defined (mirroring the RRULE spec), but it's dead — never wired up in either the organizer's UI or the code that expands the recurrence into actual bookings. Only the occurrence-**count** is functional. So "ends next month" isn't literally expressible — you'd approximate it with a count (e.g., weekly for ~4 occurrences ≈ a month).

## Bottom line for your example

**"Every Mon, Wed, Fri at 12pm, ending next month" is not achievable as one recurring series.** The closest you could get:
- Set up the event type as Weekly, interval 1, count ≈ 4–5 (to approximate "next month")
- The attendee would book **one** weekday (say, Monday) and get repeating Mondays only
- To also get Wednesdays and Fridays, you'd need the attendee to separately book those as their own starting slots on the same recurring event type — there's no way to bundle all three weekdays into a single series from one booking action.

This is a meaningfully different model than something like a Google Calendar RRULE with `BYDAY=MO,WE,FR` — cal.diy's recurrence is booker-driven and single-weekday-per-series by design, not organizer-authored multi-day patterns.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 18:01:10Z)**_

This is a **different setting** from what we discussed before — and yes, the issue accurately describes a real, current limitation.

## Confirmed: date overrides today are individual-date-only, no recurrence

- **UI**: `packages/features/schedules/components/DateOverrideInputDialog.tsx` — you get a date picker where you can click to select one or several individual calendar dates in one session, plus a time range and an "unavailable all day" toggle. There's no "repeat every week / every N weeks / until [date]" control anywhere in it.
- **Data model**: each override is stored as its own row in the `Availability` table (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma`), with an explicit `date` column — literally one row per calendar date. No RRULE-style `frequency`/`interval`/`until` fields exist on this model at all.

So to override every Saturday for 3 months today, a user really does have to individually click all ~13 Saturdays on the date picker — exactly the pain point the issue describes.

## Confirming it's not the same as "recurring events"

Correct — these are two completely separate, non-overlapping systems:

| | **Date overrides** (this issue) | **Recurring events** (what we discussed earlier) |
|---|---|---|
| Affects | The organizer's underlying **availability** (when they're bookable at all) | How a **booking** repeats after an attendee books it |
| Data model | `Availability.date` (one row per explicit date) | `EventType.recurringEvent` (RRULE-style: freq/interval/count) |
| UI | `DateOverrideInputDialog.tsx` | `RecurringEventController.tsx` |

They share no code, no schema fields, no components. So this issue is correctly scoped — it's proposing recurrence support for a feature that genuinely has none today, and it's not something the recurring-events feature already covers.

**Feasibility-wise**, this is actually a reasonably contained addition, similar in shape to earlier features we scoped: you'd extend the `Availability`/override data model to optionally store a recurrence rule (reusing the same RRULE pattern already established for recurring events, so there's a direct precedent to follow), add repeat/end-date controls to `DateOverrideInputDialog.tsx`, and have the override-saving logic expand the rule into the individual date rows at save time (or resolve it lazily when computing availability). Want me to scope that out in more depth, or is confirming the issue's premise all you needed right now?

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 18:21:50Z)**_

**No — not currently.** This fork explicitly removed the feature that provided exactly this capability.

## What used to provide this

cal.com has a **Workflows** feature (email/SMS reminders triggered before or after a booking, with a configurable time offset like "30 minutes before event start"). But in this repo, migration `packages/prisma/migrations/20260319000000_drop_workflow_tables/migration.sql` **deliberately dropped it** — the SQL comment literally says `"-- Drop workflow-related tables and columns (EE feature cleanup)"`.

That migration removed:
- The `Workflow`, `WorkflowStep`, `WorkflowReminder` tables (and several junction tables)
- All the trigger-event/action enums (`WorkflowTriggerEvents`, `WorkflowActions`, etc.)

I confirmed there's no leftover UI or backend code for it either — no `packages/features/*/workflows` directory remains. (There's a file named `packages/emails/workflow-email-service.ts`, but despite the name it's unrelated — it just handles feedback emails, monthly digest emails, and out-of-office redirect notifications, not event reminders.)

## What this means practically

- **No "remind me 30 minutes before" setting exists anywhere in cal.diy today** — for organizers or attendees.
- The only automatic emails that still fire are the built-in booking confirmation/cancellation/reschedule emails (`packages/emails/`), which aren't configurable reminders — just fixed transactional notifications tied to booking state changes, not a timer before the event starts.

This was almost certainly stripped out because Workflows was a cal.com **Enterprise Edition (EE)** feature — the comment "EE feature cleanup" suggests this fork removed EE-gated functionality rather than this being an accidental gap. If you wanted to add this back, it would mean either restoring the dropped schema/feature from upstream cal.com, or building a simpler reminder mechanism from scratch (a scheduled job checking upcoming bookings + a notification-timing setting) — happy to scope either path if you're interested.

3	You are a senior Cal.diy engineer working in a Yarn/Turbo monorepo. You prioritize type safety, security, and small, reviewable diffs.
4	
5	## Do
6	
7	- Use `select` instead of `include` in Prisma queries for performance and security
8	- Use `import type { X }` for TypeScript type imports
9	- Use early returns to reduce nesting: `if (!booking) return null;`
10	- Use `ErrorWithCode` for errors in non-tRPC files (services, repositories, utilities); use `TRPCError` only in tRPC routers
11	- Use conventional commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`
12	- Create PRs in draft mode by default
13	- Run `yarn type-check:ci --force` before concluding CI failures are unrelated to your changes
14	- Import directly from source files, not barrel files (e.g., `@calcom/ui/components/button` not `@calcom/ui`)
15	- Add translations to `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json` for all UI strings
16	- Use `date-fns` or native `Date` instead of Day.js when timezone awareness isn't needed
17	- Put permission checks in `page.tsx`, never in `layout.tsx`
18	- Use `ast-grep` for searching if available; otherwise use `rg` (ripgrep), then fall back to `grep`
19	- Use Biome for formatting and linting
20	- Only add code comments that explain **why**, not **what** — see [code comment guidelines](agents/rules/quality-code-comments.md)
21	
22	
23	## Don't
24	
25	- Never use `as any` - use proper type-safe solutions instead
26	- Never expose `credential.key` field in API responses or queries
27	- Never commit secrets or API keys
28	- Never modify `*.generated.ts` files directly - they're created by app-store-cli
29	- Never put business logic in repositories - that belongs in Services
30	- Never use barrel imports from index.ts files
31	- Never skip running type checks before pushing
32	- Never create large PRs (>500 lines or >10 files) - split them instead
33	- Never add comments that simply restate what the code does (e.g., `// Get the user` above a `getUser()` call)
34	
35	## PR Size Guidelines
36	
37	Large PRs are difficult to review, prone to errors, and slow down the development process. Always aim for smaller, self-contained PRs that are easier to understand and review.
38	
39	### Size Limits
40	
41	- **Lines changed**: Keep PRs under 500 lines of code (additions + deletions)
42	- **Files changed**: Keep PRs under 10 code files
43	- **Single responsibility**: Each PR should do one thing well
44	
45	**Note**: These limits apply to code files only. Non-code files like documentation (README.md, CHANGELOG.md), lock files (yarn.lock, package-lock.json), and auto-generated files are excluded from the count.
46	
47	### How to Split Large Changes
48	
49	When a task requires extensive changes, break it into multiple PRs:
50	
51	1. **By layer**: Separate database/schema changes, backend logic, and frontend UI into different PRs
52	2. **By feature component**: Split a feature into its constituent parts (e.g., API endpoint PR, then UI PR, then integration PR)
53	3. **By refactor vs feature**: Do preparatory refactoring in a separate PR before adding new functionality
54	4. **By dependency order**: Create PRs in the order they can be merged (base infrastructure first, then features that depend on it)
55	
56	### Examples of Good PR Splits
57	
58	**Instead of one large "Add booking notifications" PR:**
59	- PR 1: Add notification preferences schema and migration
60	- PR 2: Add notification service and API endpoints
61	- PR 3: Add notification UI components
62	- PR 4: Integrate notifications into booking flow
63	
64	**Instead of one large "Refactor calendar sync" PR:**
65	- PR 1: Extract calendar sync logic into dedicated service
66	- PR 2: Add new calendar provider abstraction
67	- PR 3: Migrate existing providers to new abstraction
68	- PR 4: Add new calendar provider support
69	
70	### Benefits of Smaller PRs
71	
72	- Faster review cycles and quicker feedback
73	- Easier to identify and fix issues
74	- Lower risk of merge conflicts
75	- Simpler to revert if problems arise
76	- Better git history and easier debugging
77	
78	## Commands
79	
80	See [agents/commands.md](agents/commands.md) for full reference. Key commands:
81	
82	```bash
83	yarn type-check:ci --force  # Type check (always run before pushing)
84	yarn biome check --write .  # Lint and format
85	TZ=UTC yarn test            # Run unit tests
86	yarn prisma generate        # Regenerate types after schema changes
87	```
88	
89	
90	## Boundaries
91	
92	### Always do
93	- Run type check on changed files before committing
94	- Run relevant tests before pushing
95	- Use `select` in Prisma queries
96	- Follow conventional commits for PR titles
97	- Run Biome before pushing
98	
99	### Ask first
100	- Adding new dependencies
101	- Schema changes to `packages/prisma/schema.prisma`
102	- Changes affecting multiple packages
103	- Deleting files
104	- Running full build or E2E suites
105	
106	### Never do
107	- Commit secrets, API keys, or `.env` files
108	- Expose `credential.key` in any query
109	- Use `as any` type casting
110	- Force push or rebase shared branches
111	- Modify generated files directly
112	
113	## Project Structure
114	
115	```
116	apps/web/                    # Main Next.js application
117	packages/prisma/             # Database schema (schema.prisma) and migrations
118	packages/trpc/               # tRPC API layer (routers in server/routers/)
119	packages/ui/                 # Shared UI components
120	packages/features/           # Feature-specific code
121	packages/app-store/          # Third-party integrations
122	packages/lib/                # Shared utilities
123	```
124	
125	### Key files
126	- Routes: `apps/web/app/` (App Router)
127	- Database schema: `packages/prisma/schema.prisma`
128	- tRPC routers: `packages/trpc/server/routers/`
129	- Translations: `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`
130	- Workflow constants: `packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/constants.ts`
131	
132	## Tech Stack
133	
134	- **Framework**: Next.js 13+ (App Router in some areas)
135	- **Language**: TypeScript (strict)
136	- **Database**: PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM
137	- **API**: tRPC for type-safe APIs
138	- **Auth**: NextAuth.js
139	- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS
140	- **Testing**: Vitest (unit), Playwright (E2E)
141	- **i18n**: next-i18next
142	
143	## Code Examples
144	
145	### Good error handling
146	
147	```typescript
148	// Good - Descriptive error with context
149	throw new Error(`Unable to create booking: User ${userId} has no available time slots for ${date}`);
150	
151	// Bad - Generic error
152	throw new Error("Booking failed");
153	```
154	
155	For which error class to use (`ErrorWithCode` vs `TRPCError`) and concrete examples, see [quality-error-handling](agents/rules/quality-error-handling.md).
156	
157	### Good Prisma query
158	
159	```typescript
160	// Good - Use select for performance and security
161	const booking = await prisma.booking.findFirst({
162	  select: {
163	    id: true,
164	    title: true,
165	    user: {
166	      select: {
167	        id: true,
168	        name: true,
169	        email: true,
170	      }
171	    }
172	  }
173	});
174	
175	// Bad - Include fetches all fields including sensitive ones
176	const booking = await prisma.booking.findFirst({
177	  include: { user: true }
178	});
179	```
180	
181	### Good imports
182	
183	```typescript
184	// Good - Type imports and direct paths
185	import type { User } from "@prisma/client";
186	import { Button } from "@calcom/ui/components/button";
187	
188	// Bad - Regular import for types, barrel imports
189	import { User } from "@prisma/client";
190	import { Button } from "@calcom/ui";
191	```
192	
193	### API v2 Imports (apps/api/v2)
194	
195	When importing from `@calcom/features` or `@calcom/trpc` into `apps/api/v2`, **do not import directly** because the API v2 app's `tsconfig.json` doesn't have path mappings for these modules, which causes "module not found" errors.
196	
197	Instead, re-export from `packages/platform/libraries/index.ts` and import from `@calcom/platform-libraries`:
198	
199	```typescript
200	// Step 1: In packages/platform/libraries/index.ts, add the export
201	export { ProfileRepository } from "@calcom/features/profile/repositories/ProfileRepository";
202	
203	// Step 2: In apps/api/v2, import from platform-libraries
204	import { ProfileRepository } from "@calcom/platform-libraries";
205	
206	// Bad - Direct import causes module not found error in apps/api/v2
207	import { ProfileRepository } from "@calcom/features/profile/repositories/ProfileRepository";
208	```
209	
210	## PR Checklist
211	
212	- [ ] Title follows conventional commits: `feat(scope): description`
213	- [ ] Type check passes: `yarn type-check:ci --force`
214	- [ ] Lint passes: `yarn lint:fix`
215	- [ ] Relevant tests pass
216	- [ ] Diff is small and focused (<500 lines, <10 files)
217	- [ ] No secrets or API keys committed
218	- [ ] UI strings added to translation files
219	- [ ] Created as draft PR
220	
221	## When Stuck
222	
223	- Ask a clarifying question before making large speculative changes
224	- Propose a short plan for complex tasks
225	- Open a draft PR with notes if unsure about approach
226	- Fix type errors before test failures - they're often the root cause
227	- Run `yarn prisma generate` if you see missing enum/type errors
228	
229	## Spec-Driven Development (Opt-In)
230	
231	For complex features, you can use spec-driven development when explicitly requested.
232	
233	**To enable:** Tell the AI "use spec-driven development" or "follow the spec workflow"
234	
235	See [SPEC-WORKFLOW.md](SPEC-WORKFLOW.md) for the full workflow documentation.
236

## Identity framing (top)
Sets the persona: "senior Cal.diy engineer," prioritizing type safety, security, small diffs. This isn't fluff — it's calibrating the *default risk tolerance* for everything below (e.g., why PRs must stay small, why schema changes need permission first).

## Do / Don't — the two rule lists
These are concrete, greppable conventions specific to this codebase, not generic advice:
- **`select` over `include` in Prisma** — we saw this exact pattern in practice when researching bookings (`ctx.prisma...select: {...}`); `include` fetches every field including sensitive ones like `credential.key`, which the Don't list separately calls out as never-expose.
- **`ErrorWithCode` vs `TRPCError`** — a layer-specific rule: services/repos/utils throw `ErrorWithCode`, only tRPC routers throw `TRPCError`. Mixing these up is an easy mistake in a codebase where routers call into services.
- **No barrel imports** (`@calcom/ui/components/button`, not `@calcom/ui`) — this matters for build performance in a monorepo this size; a barrel `index.ts` re-exporting everything forces bundlers to potentially pull in far more than one component.
- **Never modify `*.generated.ts`** — directly relevant to what we saw in `packages/app-store/` (the `apps.schemas.generated.ts`, `apps.metadata.generated.ts`, etc. files that were sitting modified in your git status). Those are produced by `app-store-cli`; hand-editing them is a footgun since the next codegen run silently overwrites your changes.

## PR Size Guidelines
Hard caps (<500 lines, <10 files) plus a playbook for splitting bigger work — by layer (schema → backend → UI), by feature slice, or refactor-then-feature. This is the same shape of reasoning I used when scoping the sidebar unsaved-changes dialog earlier (core plumbing vs. each additional guard point as separate, smaller work).

Points to `agents/commands.md` for the full list, but inlines the four you'll use constantly — notably `TZ=UTC yarn test`, which matches exactly what we ran together (with the added `--maxWorkers=4` your machine needed).

## Boundaries — the permission model
This is the most operationally important section for how I behave day to day:
- **Always do** without asking: type-check changed files, run relevant tests, use `select`, Biome.
- **Ask first**: new dependencies, schema changes, cross-package changes, deleting files, full build/E2E runs. This is a stricter, codebase-specific layer on top of my own general "ask before risky actions" defaults — e.g., it flags *any* `schema.prisma` change as ask-first, not just destructive ones.
- **Never**: secrets, `credential.key` exposure, `as any`, force-push/rebase shared branches, editing generated files.

1	# Contributing to Cal.diy
2	
3	> **Important:** Cal.diy is a community-driven, open-source fork of Cal.com. Contributions made here **do not** get merged into Cal.com's production service — Cal.com is now closed-source. This repo is maintained independently by the community under the MIT license.
4	
5	Contributions are what make the open source community such an amazing place to learn, inspire, and create. Any contributions you make are **greatly appreciated**.
6	
7	## House Rules (for PRs and Issues)
8	
9	### 👥 Prevent Work Duplication
10	
11	Before submitting a new issue or PR, check if it already exists in the [Issues](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/issues) or [Pull Requests](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/pulls).
12	
13	### ✅ Work Only on Approved Issues
14	
15	For feature requests, please wait for a core team member to approve and remove the `🚨 needs approval` label before you start coding or submitting a PR.
16	
17	For bugs, security, performance, documentation, etc., you can start coding immediately—even if the `🚨 needs approval` label is present.
18	
19	We highly value new feature ideas, but to maintain consistency in the product direction, they must go through a review and approval process.
20	
21	### 🚫 Don’t Just Drop a Link
22	
23	Avoid posting third-party links (e.g., Slack threads or Linear tickets) without context. A GitHub issue or PR should stand on its own—reviewers shouldn’t have to chase information across multiple tools to understand the context.
24	
25	### 👀 Think Like a Reviewer
26	
27	Put yourself in the reviewer’s shoes. What would you want to know if reading this for the first time? Are there key decisions, goals, or constraints that need clarification? Does the PR assume knowledge that isn’t obvious? Are there related issues or previous PRs that should be linked?
28	
29	### 🧵 Bring in Context from Private Channels
30	
31	If the task originated from a private conversation (e.g., Slack), take a moment to extract the relevant details and include them in the GitHub issue or PR. Avoid sharing sensitive information, but make sure important reasoning is captured.
32	
33	> Example:  
34	> “A user requested feature X to solve problem Y. I considered approaches A, B, and C, but chose C for the following reasons…”
35	
36	### 📚 Treat It Like Documentation
37	
38	GitHub is a shared source of truth. Every issue and PR contributes to the long-term understanding of the codebase. Write clearly enough that someone—possibly you—can revisit it months later and still understand what happened and why.
39	
40	### ✅ Summarize Your PR at the Top
41	
42	Even if the code changes are minor or self-explanatory, a short written summary helps reviewers quickly understand the intent. You can use GitHub Copilot’s auto-summarize feature, but make sure to verify it for accuracy and relevance.
43	
44	### 🔗 Use GitHub Keywords to Auto-Link Issues
45	
46	Use phrases like “Closes #123” or “Fixes #456” in your PR descriptions. This automatically links your PR to the related issue and closes it once merged—keeping everything traceable and organized.
47	
48	### 🧪 Mention What Was Tested (and How)
49	
50	Explain how you validated your changes. It doesn’t need to be exhaustive—just enough to give reviewers confidence that things were tested and work as expected.
51	
52	> Example:  
53	> “Tested locally with mock data and confirmed the flow works on staging.”
54	
55	### 🧠 Assume Future-You Won’t Remember
56	
57	Write with the future in mind. If there are trade-offs, edge cases, or temporary workarounds, document them clearly so they don’t get lost or misinterpreted later.

100	## File Naming Conventions
101	
102	To ensure consistency and make files easy to fuzzy-find, we follow the naming conventions below for **services**, **repositories**, and other class-based files.
103	
104	### Repository Files
105	
106	- Repository class files must include the `Repository` suffix.
107	- If the repository is backed by a specific technology (e.g. Prisma), prefix the filename and class name with it.
108	- File name must match the exported class exactly (PascalCase).
109	
110	**Pattern:**
111	
112	`Prisma<Entity>Repository.ts`
113	
114	**Examples:**
115	
116	```ts
117	// File: PrismaAppRepository.ts
118	export class PrismaAppRepository { ... }
119	
120	// File: PrismaMembershipRepository.ts
121	export class PrismaMembershipRepository { ... }
122	```
123	
124	This avoids ambiguous filenames like app.ts and improves discoverability in editors.
125	
126	### Service Files
127	
128	- Service class files must include the Service suffix.
129	- File name should be in PascalCase, matching the exported class.
130	- Keep naming specific — avoid generic names like AppService.ts.
131	
132	**Pattern:**
133	
134	`<Entity>Service.ts`
135	
136	**Examples:**
137	
138	```ts
139	// File: MembershipService.ts
140	export class MembershipService { ... }
141	
142	// File: HashedLinkService.ts
143	export class HashedLinkService { ... }
144	```
145	
146	**Note:**
147	
148	- New files must avoid dot-suffixes like .service.ts or .repository.ts; these will be migrated from the existing codebase progressively.
149	- We still reserve suffixes such as .test.ts, .spec.ts, and .types.ts for their respective use cases.

193	## Making a Pull Request
194	
195	### Keep PRs Small and Focused
196	
197	Large PRs are difficult to review and more prone to errors. We strongly encourage smaller, self-contained PRs:
198	
199	- **Size limits**: Keep PRs under 500 lines of code changed and under 10 code files modified (excludes documentation, lock files, and auto-generated files)
200	- **Single responsibility**: Each PR should address one concern (one feature, one bug fix, or one refactor)
201	- **Split large changes**: If your task requires extensive changes, break it into multiple PRs that can be reviewed and merged independently
202	
203	**How to split large changes:**
204	- Separate database/schema changes from application logic
205	- Split frontend and backend changes when possible
206	- Do preparatory refactoring in a separate PR before adding new features
207	- Create PRs in dependency order (infrastructure first, then features)
208	
209	### PR Checklist
210	
211	- Be sure to [check the "Allow edits from maintainers" option](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/allowing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork) when creating your PR. (This option isn't available if you're [contributing from a fork belonging to an organization](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/5634))
212	- If your PR refers to or fixes an issue, add `refs #XXX` or `fixes #XXX` to the PR description. Replace `XXX` with the respective issue number. See more about [linking a pull request to an issue](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue).

`CONTRIBUTING.md` is the repo's PR/issue etiquette guide — distinct from `AGENTS.md` (which governs how an *AI agent* should write code) in that this one is aimed at *human* contributor behavior and process, though several rules overlap (PR size limits appear in both, verbatim).

## The disclaimer at the top (read this first)

> "Cal.diy is a community-driven, open-source fork of Cal.com... Cal.com is now closed-source. This repo is maintained independently by the community under the MIT license."

This is important context for a student: you're working in an **independent educational fork**, not staging changes for the real cal.com product. Cal.com itself went closed-source, so this repo exists as a standalone MIT-licensed continuation for teaching/community purposes.

## House Rules — process norms for issues/PRs

Eight numbered-by-emoji conventions, mostly about *communication quality* rather than code:
- **Prevent duplication** — search existing issues/PRs first.
- **Work only on approved issues** — feature requests need a core-team member to remove a `🚨 needs approval` label before you start; bugs/security/perf/docs can be started immediately. This is a gate specifically to protect product direction on features, not on fixes.
- **Don't just drop a link** — a PR/issue must stand alone; no "see this Slack thread" without extracting the actual content.
- **Think like a reviewer** / **treat it like documentation** / **assume future-you won't remember** — three restatements of the same idea: write for a stranger (or forgetful future-you) reading this in six months, not for someone with your current context.
- **Summarize at the top**, **use `Closes #123` keywords**, **mention what you tested** — concrete mechanical habits for PR descriptions.

## Priorities table

Maps issue *type* to expected urgency: minor/non-core → low, confusing-but-functional UX → medium, core features (booking page, availability, timezone calc) → high, core bugs (login, booking, emails broken) → urgent. Useful for triaging if you're picking an issue to work on.

## File Naming Conventions — the part with real teeth for code you write here

This is the one section with concrete, checkable rules:
- **Repositories**: `Prisma<Entity>Repository.ts`, class name must match filename exactly (PascalCase) — e.g. `PrismaAppRepository.ts` exporting `class PrismaAppRepository`. This directly explains a pattern you'd notice while exploring `packages/features/` — repository files are prefixed by their backing tech, not left as ambiguous names like `app.ts`.
- **Services**: `<Entity>Service.ts`, specific not generic (avoid `AppService.ts`) — e.g. `MembershipService.ts`, `HashedLinkService.ts`. This lines up with `AGENTS.md`'s rule that business logic belongs in Services, not Repositories.
- **No new dot-suffix files** (`.service.ts`, `.repository.ts`) — existing ones will be migrated progressively, but don't add more. `.test.ts`/`.spec.ts`/`.types.ts` are still fine, those are reserved for their actual purpose.

## Developing / Building / Testing / Linting

Mostly pointers to the README rather than self-contained instructions — notice `yarn build` and `yarn lint` are given as plain commands here, whereas everything we actually ran together used `node .yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs <cmd>` because of the corepack bug on your machine. This doc doesn't know about that; it assumes plain `yarn` already works, which is exactly `students.md`'s job to patch over for Windows.

## Making a Pull Request

Repeats the PR size limits from `AGENTS.md` almost verbatim (< 500 lines, < 10 files, single responsibility, split by layer/frontend-backend/refactor-then-feature) — so this rule is enforced from two independent documents, which is a strong signal it's taken seriously here.

**One thing worth flagging, similar to the stale references we found in `AGENTS.md`:** the PR checklist talks about checking "Allow edits from maintainers" and links to GitHub's *forking* documentation — but recall `students.md` explicitly told your class to use a **branch-based workflow**, not forks, specifically because everyone already has write access to the shared repo. That checklist item is boilerplate carried over from a generic open-source contributing guide and doesn't quite apply to your class's actual workflow (there's no fork to enable maintainer-edits on, since you're pushing branches directly to the shared repo). Worth keeping in mind if that checklist confuses you later.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-16 01:30:39Z)**_

No — this isn't a UI component at all. `event-types.ts` in `packages/prisma/selects/` is a **database query helper**, not something that renders or validates anything. It sits purely in the data-fetching layer.

## What it actually does

Each export here (`baseEventTypeSelect`, `bookEventTypeSelect`, `availiblityPageEventTypeSelect`) is a **Prisma `select` object** — a reusable list of "which columns to fetch" for an `EventType` query, typed against `Prisma.EventTypeSelect` so TypeScript catches typos or renamed fields at compile time. This is the concrete pattern behind the `AGENTS.md` rule we just went through: *"Use `select` instead of `include`... for performance and security."* Instead of writing out the same 15–20 field list inline every time some tRPC handler queries an event type, it's centralized here and imported wherever needed, e.g.:

```ts
prisma.eventType.findFirst({ where: { id }, select: bookEventTypeSelect })
```

`description` on line 6/26/77 is just one field name in these lists — it tells Prisma "include this column in the result," nothing more.

## Why there are three different selects

Each one is shaped for a different consumer, fetching only what that specific page/flow actually needs:
- **`baseEventTypeSelect`** — a minimal common set (id, title, description, price, etc.), likely reused as a base for other selects.
- **`bookEventTypeSelect`** — for the actual **booking page** (attendee-facing), so it pulls in `locations`, `bookingFields`, `users` (host info), `team` branding — everything needed to render the booker.
- **`availiblityPageEventTypeSelect`** — for **availability computation**, so it pulls in `schedule`, `timeZone`, `minimumBookingNotice`, buffers, `slotInterval` — everything needed to calculate open slots, and notably *doesn't* need `bookingFields` since it's not rendering a form.

## Where rendering and validation actually happen instead

- **Rendering the description in the UI**: wherever the component that receives this query result displays it — e.g. the booking page component would receive `description` as a prop/field and render it in JSX. That's a separate file entirely (a `.tsx` component under `apps/web/modules/bookings/` or similar), not this one.
- **Validating the description field**: that's a Zod schema, likely in `packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts` or wherever the event-type update form's input schema lives (probably enforcing something like a max length) — again, a completely different file from this one.

So `event-types.ts` is the *"what to fetch from the database"* layer — one of three separate concerns (fetch → validate → render) that are deliberately kept in different files in this codebase.
